I was skeptical playing this game for fear they would ruin Mad Max and especially the character of Max. BUT THEY DID NOT! This is coming from someone who grew up highly influenced by Mad Max in the 80s. Especially Road Warrior. For those of us who grew up watching and letting our imaginations run wild living in this post-apocolyptic world, this game is your chance to experience it.
Here's my take:
PROS:
- Max stays true to his character.
- Many elements taken from the movies to capture the style.
- The love of water and gasoline
- Character and car upgrades/modifications
- Atmosphere
- Sound design and music (used effectively)
- Gameplay
- Graphics
- Voice talent
- Writing and script
- Length (depending on how you play)
- Insane antagonists
- Storms (freaky watching them come at you from the distance)
- Lots to do (don't just do the story missions)
- Car chases/fights are freakin' fun!
- Hand-to-hand and melee fights were really fun. Best I've ever played in 3rd person so far.
- Never once got stuck in the crazy terrain or debris.
- Minimal glitches
- Minimal cut scenes and when they happen they are effective.
- Car POV!! In my opinion, a must for the true experience.
- The ending
CONS:
- Driving off a cliff doesn't do near as much damage as it should (or should just kill you).
- Character movement on rocky terrain is problematic but not as bad as other 3rd person games I've played.
- Head-on collisions should be catastrophic
- Black screen glitch (I solved it but see below)
I actually had a hard time coming up with cons. But the car physics is probably the way it is to maintain a level of fun instead of frustration.
ISSUES:
Who knows what the problem was exactly. Perhaps my Nvidia GPU but I experienced black screens when launching or trying to quit the game. As a user mentioned in the forums, using GeForce Experience settings for the game, go window/borderless mode instead of fullscreen. This fixed it.
Personal preference to experience the game:
- Keyboard+mouse for Max and Xbox 360 controller for the car
- POV in the car
I recommend it to those who have the patience for scavenging and driving around and just allowing yourself to get into the enviornment. If you like Borderlands, you probably won't get frustrated with the looting/scavenging flow. I could see it being frustrating to certain types of gamers who need action action action. But driving is the real beauty of the game. And I think they balanced the desolate environment mixed with action pretty good. I went 30 hrs off course from the story missions just looting and ridding the different territories of clans. Lots to do and different things to do to break it up.
Total gameplay for me was 72 hrs and still lots to do left over. After you finish the game, if you want, you can still continue doing this-and-that but I was completely satisfied with the ending I called it quits.

Wow. This game took me by surprise. First off when I started out in the game, I thought "These graphics look ridiculously good". Then I wondered around on foot and completed the first set of missions until I was able to drive the car. And that's when I drove around and thought "This world is huge!". But that was before I checked the map for the first time and realized that the part that I thought was huge was only one twentieth of the entire map. Whoa. I didn't like the combat at first but as I began upgrading max, I began to like the combat way better, because of all the moves you can have max learn. I also love how much the game plays like the movies. It really feels like an entirely new mad max sequel. Really really good game that I would totally recommend purchasing if you love games like Batman Arkham or Tomb Raider. The only thing that I found a problem was the controls feel a little bit clunky to me but then again that might just be me idk. I found the story very deep and actually pretty emotional. It really proves to the audience how Max is so detached from the world; he loses everything. The death races are a bit annoying to do with a keyboard but they are all pretty much optional. There is TONS of extras in this game to give any hand to hand combat-lover, gear head, lore fanatics or completionist a lot of replay value. If I were to add one thing to the game it would probably be a new game plus option, that way, my scrap, upgrades, and progress through the map/outposts would carry over too each new game. I would love a feature like this because after you complete the main story/side quests, the extra stuff to collect in the game may get a little repetitive/grindy for some people, but I was able to look past this due to the diverse vehicle/hand to hand combat. Overall, 9/10 game. Definitely an experience to remember and one of the few recent games I've played with a story that really stuck with me.

HITMAN Episode 1 Review:
As a big pain in the♥♥♥♥♥that I can be when it comes to picking up the little details that I dislike, those aside, I ♥♥♥♥ING LOVE Showstopper. Seriously I was Very skeptic week before its release (maybe that way its better?) but to my surprise I turned out to be one of the best Hitman experiences I ever had. Simply put -I can't stop playing it.
Yes there are problems like:
Allways online DRM and poor optimization (which hopefully will be patched soon).
Lack of blood with some animations, some sound glitches - those are all can be fixed with upcoming updates aswel.
Take in mind that IOI is listening to us. Remember how we all wanted, now famous, "Baby-face 47" to be gone? IOI completely changed his face model to look exactly like in CGI trailer and I dare to say that now its the best looking 47's face model we ever had.
Seriously, nitpicking aside, from gameplay and level design perspective - this is all that I could have ever wished from a Hitman game, considering what Blood Money worshiper I am.
Showstopper is:
MASSIVE and by that I mean that pretty much every space / room it in has its purpose in the level - its not just an empty space for the sake of beeing "space".
Insanely detailed and rich with content. I mean I play it on PC with all settings maxed out to Ultra and boy oh boy it looks SHARP! Visually its stunning, I cant find better word for it to describe. It literally took me about 3-4 hrs on my first playtrough to figure out how to eliminate my targets. I was simply lost in the immense amount of on-going things/events around me. And I still am.
The world feels like it's trully alive. If you take your time and dont rush it, you can hear so many interesting stories and even Easter Eggs told by NPCs - and thank God those are not cheesy Absolution 'jokes'. Really love all the living feel of the level.
It offers Ridiculous replay value for a price tag of 13 Euros (in a good way ofc) - according to my Steam account I have already spent over 12 hrs in-game and I didn't even felt it. That's how good it is for me. I haven't even done more 40% of whats possible in this first Episode, nor even started doing my 'perfectionist' speedruns yet. I don't want to rush myself just yet because I feel like it would be a mistake hah!
So far, with best things yet to come (Elusive targets and rewards) - I would rate this first episode with a VERY SOLID 8+/10. Once server problems will be taken care off and optimisation patches released - Im sure I could easily rate it 9/10 or even 10/10

Max Payne, is a unique creation. A highly difficult third person shooter, that is extremely dark in it's gritty and noir atmosphere. The game would be nigh impossible if it were not for the bullet time mechanic; which allows you to dodge in slow motion to avoid bullets (and retaliate). Clocking into 7 hours, you'll be blasting your way through Max's bitter story. The movement and shooting mechanics are fluid and allow  freedom of movement during combat. The story and level is expertly woven together with intersections of narrated graphic novel in a truly noir fashion. The game certainly shows it's age in this time. Though the story and atmosphere is timeless, the game's graphics and stiff animations certainly show it's age. This deducts slightly from the overall atmosphere of the game and graphic-addicts may find Max Payne less immersive.
Overall Max Payne is a excellent and unique experience, although the age may affect the immersion, the quality of the writing will never fade.
8/10

Games can have good story. Games can make you empathize. Max Payne and its sequel are proof of this. Max Payne the game introduced us to the concept of Bullet Time and action gaming and cinema have benefited greatly from it. I played the Playstation 2 version of this game years ago and always enjoyed it, but found the PC version ultimately more fun to play. MP is a crowning achivement in third-person shooter gaming, but the story doesn't end here. When you're done with this game, move on to the sequel without delay.
Absolute classic and has aged remarkably well in the last 11 years. With the threequel round the corner, it's definitely worth revisiting.

Oxygen Not Included is a great start. It looks very polished; the art is delightful and expressive, the interface is generally clear and intuitive, and the audio is exceptionally pleasant. There are also a set of interesting challenges to overcome, and learning how to do that feels satisfyingly realistic. You have to learn how to stuff your colonists with all the things they need:
For each of these elements, there are several potential solutions, with their own trade-offs in terms of resources. Generating oxygen using algae is great, but you'll burn through your supply of algae rather quickly. Climbing the tech tree nets you more and more efficient problem-solvers, but creates its own problems; now you need electricity to power your research. Eventually, you cascade through a chain of problem-solution-new problem-new solution, and that's the game.
The issue is, that's all there is to it. Despite the complexity and sophistication of the simulation, there's just no more than four hops along any particular resource chain. Running through them all can take a bit of time if you're a perfectionist, but as yet there's no real reason to. There's no story, no broader progression, and no way to define any but self-imposed challenges. There are also some problems with illogical or impossible reactions: generate hydrogen and oxygen from water for 120 watts of power, burn that hydrogen in a generator, and get more than 500 watts of power back, without burning the oxygen or generating any water. Mysterious!
That said, development is ongoing, the price is right, and the style is delightful. It's recommendable now, but it may become essential later.

After several hour of play the missions quickly get repetitive. Trading and mining get boring even quicker. The real challenge of the game is capturing enemy ships (and it is the only way to make enough money to advance in the game).
The faction system didn't much much sense to me, and didn't seem very important as it was just goodies vs badies in the end.
Near the end game there was nothing to spend your cash on. The weapons at the end of the game really aren't much better than what you get 20% into the game.
The game crashes from time to time, but not enough to ruin the game thanks to the auto-save feature. It is a 32bit only game and seems to run out of virtual RAM. The developers should have also included a 64bit executable in the install package.
So, good fun for maybe 20 hours.
Some suggestions as to what would have made this a great game.
- Some ship customisation (and why can't I see the weapon arcs)
- More variety in the  enemy ships (maybe some boss ships)
- Some random system wide events. Not just random pirates
- The hacking (and anti-hacking) features making some sense. I didn't get hacked ever, but had zero protection.
- More high end weapons and gear
- The galaxy having low and high level sections rather than being seemingly mostly uniform. At the moment sectors are either friendly or impossibly hard.  I never found any netural sectors.

I have one major criticism for this game: It actively dissuades you from continuing to play it.
Once you beat it in a particular route, odds are you've seen everything you can see in that route. The puzzles and combat aren't worth playing more than once, and the jokes are old the first time you finish the game. Once you get the best ending, you're actually told to not play again, and if you get the worst ending, the other endings are permanently affected. You're dissuaded from playing the game once you beat it once, and dissuaded even more depending on how you beat it.
That aside, I think Undertale is a very well-made game that is worth buying and playing for yourself.

This is the most overhyped game I can ever remember playing.  It's not only a step back from the first Borderlands, it's uninteresting, frustrating, and tedious.  There is a large amount of content in the game, but overall the experience isn't worth more than $5, in my opinion.  The enemies are cheap, overpowered, and unintelligent.  If you're not fighting monsters that can destroy 90% of your HP/Shield in 1-2 hits, you're fighting invisible teleporting monsters that move faster than your bullets.  Seriously, the speed of bullets in this game will make you feel like a monster 100 feet away is actually a mile away.
I'll sum up the story in one word:  boring.  Every single story mission sounds straight forward to begin with, but when you reach your objective, 100% of the time something will go wrong and you'll end up backtracking and doing a whole bunch of other stuff to accomplish what seem like simple goals.  Menial tasks is story missions.  Unbelievable.  There were three times in the course of hundreds of lines of dialogue that made me laugh.  90% of the dialogue was written with the intent of being funny, but it's not.  The "comedy" feels forced and unnatural.  The game tries way too hard to be comedic and the whole effort just seems like the writers were trying to manufacture memes.  The most memorable character from the first borderlands is barely even featured in this game and has become just another uninteresting NPC.
This is not an RPG (it has quests but you might as well call every game where you fetch a key an RPG), it's an FPS where there is no strategy in taking down your opponents.  More importantly, it's a loot-grinding game much like Diablo 3.  I hope you like Twitter, because if you want weapons that will actually let you progress through the story without doing dozens of side-quests, you'll need to watch their Twitter account so you can get good loot.  In the course of this game, I saw two purple rarity weapons.  Follow them on Twitter and you can get a key that will give you more than that.  Don't want to do that?  Hope you like side quests.
Let's talk again about the enemies.  Invisible, teleporting enemies that can also run faster than your bullets do not make good enemies.  They are annoying ones.  There are probably a dozen, maybe as many as 18 different enemy types (not counting bosses).  Many of the enemies will simply spawn all around you when you enter an area.  That makes the game challenging, but not in a fun "I can do this!" kind of way.  It's more like, "Why the hell did all of these dudes emerge from huts once they had me surrounded?  Why can't I enter or blow up the huts and approach areas like I don't want to be killed?  Why did anyone think this would be fun?"  The vast majority of the encounters you will face are difficult because the enemies are so much more deadly than the player.  It can take hundreds of bullets to kill a single enemy, but that same enemy may only need to hit the player twice to kill them.
The AI is almost nonexistant.  Enemies spawn all around you, occasionally take cover, and usually just walk towards the player without any regard for their own safety.  Enemies do not flank the player except by accident.  There are TONS of kamikaze enemies, but even the ones that aren't kamikazes prefer to be right in the player's face, shooting the hell out of you.  This is a good strategy for them because they are ridiculously bullet resistant, but it's cheap.  In short, the enemies are cheap and annoying in almost every instance.
The heart of this game is about loot.  99% of the loot you will see will not be an upgrade and will be sold.  In the first Borderlands, I felt like I was getting upgrades all the time.  In this game, even the big upgrades feel weak.  Elemental damage weapons are more prevalant in this sequel, but interesting weapons have been removed.  There are no shotguns (at least that I ever saw) that shoot bouncy projectiles, but there are weapons that explode when you reload them.  After the first few hours of the game, it will feel like no weapon upgrade is enough to deal with the cheapness of the enemies you will face.  You will look at the stats, you will say to yourself "Now this is what I needed!" and after 15 minutes, the weapon will feel weak again.  The guns do look VERY cool.  Too bad they're not.
The classes are just tweaks of the first game's classes.  Pathetic.  I tried really hard to like this game and was excited because I enjoyed the first Borderlands quite a lot, but I was very disappointed.
3/10 - Too much hype, cheap enemies, boring characters/story, social media is part of game design, and bad loot.  HOPE YOU LIKE TWITTER.

I was skeptical playing this game for fear they would ruin Mad Max and especially the character of Max. BUT THEY DID NOT! This is coming from someone who grew up highly influenced by Mad Max in the 80s. Especially Road Warrior. For those of us who grew up watching and letting our imaginations run wild living in this post-apocolyptic world, this game is your chance to experience it.
Here's my take:
PROS:
- Max stays true to his character.
- Many elements taken from the movies to capture the style.
- The love of water and gasoline
- Character and car upgrades/modifications
- Atmosphere
- Sound design and music (used effectively)
- Gameplay
- Graphics
- Voice talent
- Writing and script
- Length (depending on how you play)
- Insane antagonists
- Storms (freaky watching them come at you from the distance)
- Lots to do (don't just do the story missions)
- Car chases/fights are freakin' fun!
- Hand-to-hand and melee fights were really fun. Best I've ever played in 3rd person so far.
- Never once got stuck in the crazy terrain or debris.
- Minimal glitches
- Minimal cut scenes and when they happen they are effective.
- Car POV!! In my opinion, a must for the true experience.
- The ending
CONS:
- Driving off a cliff doesn't do near as much damage as it should (or should just kill you).
- Character movement on rocky terrain is problematic but not as bad as other 3rd person games I've played.
- Head-on collisions should be catastrophic
- Black screen glitch (I solved it but see below)
I actually had a hard time coming up with cons. But the car physics is probably the way it is to maintain a level of fun instead of frustration.
ISSUES:
Who knows what the problem was exactly. Perhaps my Nvidia GPU but I experienced black screens when launching or trying to quit the game. As a user mentioned in the forums, using GeForce Experience settings for the game, go window/borderless mode instead of fullscreen. This fixed it.
Personal preference to experience the game:
- Keyboard+mouse for Max and Xbox 360 controller for the car
- POV in the car
I recommend it to those who have the patience for scavenging and driving around and just allowing yourself to get into the enviornment. If you like Borderlands, you probably won't get frustrated with the looting/scavenging flow. I could see it being frustrating to certain types of gamers who need action action action. But driving is the real beauty of the game. And I think they balanced the desolate environment mixed with action pretty good. I went 30 hrs off course from the story missions just looting and ridding the different territories of clans. Lots to do and different things to do to break it up.
Total gameplay for me was 72 hrs and still lots to do left over. After you finish the game, if you want, you can still continue doing this-and-that but I was completely satisfied with the ending I called it quits.

Everything about this game suggests that its review should be in the style of a Spaghetti western, calling back to the original man squinting in the sun.
The Good
What the good means should really go without explanation.
This game really does have a lot to offer (for about 30 hours). First, it fits rather neatly into the Mad Max universe, besides the main baddy not really conforming to the timelines offered by the comics which accompanied Fury Road. The game is a prequel for Fury Road and honestly significant portions of the movie make a little more sense after playing the game. The story is overall fairly good, representing Max as he should be. The voice acting is far better than passable, and the game has a very cinematic feel.
Second, the environment is stellar. I never thought dystopian Australia could be so fun. The distances feel vast without particularly disrupting the pace of the game play. The resources feel simultaneously plentiful and sparse. every time you take having something for granted, its gone when you really need it. If you are goal and completionist oriented, this game can start to feel bare toward the end, and if you neglect sidemissions and blowing camps, it can feel chaotic all the way through but, in the end, you get the environment your playstyle provides, and that actually feels pretty fantastic.
I also really enjoyed the car, from combat to customization. I like that not only are there a variety of upgrades, but many of them come with tradeoffs, so you really need to modify your car to accomodate your current objective. Your weight(an invisible stat that has visible effects on your acceleration and handling) effects all kinds of things including how easy it is to pull down stuff. The world feels amazingly responsive to every detail of the car, and as a result the car is amazing fun to drive. Meanwhile the combat feels edgy and dangerous, with constant decision making about whether you can afford to just blow that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up with a thunderpoon or do you need to save it? The necessity of being scrupulous with resources is what keeps the combat interesting.
With all of that said, this games greatest assets is somewhat ineffiable. Its just fun. No matter what I say after this point, the game is fun. I feel like Jeremy Clarkson (of Top Gear, producer punching fame) when I say this, but no matter the problems, the game is damn fun. You won't even notice the problems for the first 10 hours. You will be too busy harpooning anything thats not nailed down, yanking off car wheels and performing an amazing back suplex on baddies to notice. Amazing. Fantastic. Fun. For no discernable reason.
The Bad
This really goes without explanation as well. There are parts of this game that, once you hit 15 hours deep, start to feel incomplete, unpolished, or just halfassed.
First and most glaring issue is the mini bosses. There are a variety of minibosses in this game, except there arent. There is one mini boss you fight 5 times with slightly different colors applied to his texture. His move set is the same, his strategy is the same. and if done properly, you can kill each and every one of them without getting touched. It kind of feels like this character was supposed to be an infrequent normal enemy, but they ran out of time to design the bosses so they just doubled his health bar and called it a day.
Second, the "ground combat". I wouldn't really call it bad per se, but its not good and anything but ugly. The combat feels tight and visceral, but suffers from the the worst parts of Assassin's creed's early issues, with the engine not quite knowing how to deal with multiple attackers. Enemy attacks are also somewhat one dimensional, with insufficient variety to keep you engaged for more than one playthrough. Max's abilities continue to develop, but enemies hit a stopping point pretty early and remain vanilla from there. So of course the solution is to throw more of them at you. Which the engine doesn't handle well. Which means you end up in no win situations where you counter a move only to be punched in the back of the head.
The Ugly
Its really hard to say anything about this visually stunning game is ugly, so my best use of this section is not talking about the visuals, but instead things about the game that end up just being disappointing without necessarily being bad.
The biggest thing here is the way Max interacts with the environment. While the environment itself is pretty stunning, it screams for a more open world feel akin to assassin's creed. So many waist high ledges and no way to climb them. It feels like you are invited to walk around within an amazing picture, but only allowed to touch the stuff colored yellow.
Another quibble is the necessity of completionist methods in order to get all the gear. Not everyone has that playstyle, and even though I do, it felt repetitive and grindy by the time I got to the third area of the game. All in all, not that big a downside because of the fun the game maintains, but downright vexing toward the end.
The standoff
All in all, this game is engaging and visually moving, but it lacks a depth I have come to expect from games of the genre. Despite that weakness, its an amazing amount of fun. I wouldn't buy it at full price, but at $10 or less, its less than a DVD and significantly more bang for the buck. Buy it next time its on sale.

Just to reitirate what many other positive reviews are saying:
"Everyone is outlining the performance issues and online DRM but not the game itself"
This Hitman is easily the best in the series, the gameplay is incredible, there are so many ways to complete missions it's actually ridiculous, we've never had this in a Hitman game, a very welcome edition to the series.
My only problem is the fact that it's episodic. If it wasn't for that this would be a contender for GOTY in my eyes.

DISCLAIMER: There have been reports of performance issues on certain rig setups. While I experienced none of them, I cannot act naive to this or forget about this. It won't affect my final rating, since I just base it off my experience, but please consider this a "wait on it till the issues are fixed" before you deal with it.
Hitman. The series is known for being a slightly over the top yet very grounded stealth series, where you go and kill terrible terrorists that would thousands if it wasn't for you, your silenced pistols, and a bunny suit. It's a fun series, though I've only really played half of Absolution beforehand, so I'm not experienced with this series. I did preorder the $15 version of this game, however, and started playing it? So how do I like it? Well, lets look.
STORY: You are Agent 47. You're sent to kill people. That's it, pretty much. Only the prologue and the Paris mission are available as of now, and there isn't much story there. It's not really that strong, but there is a small bit more than I let on, and if they expand on it more, it might be interesting. We'll have to see.
GAMEPLAY: From what I remember, same Hitman gameplay as the last. You start off at a certain place (you can unlock where in the challenges menu), choose the gear you go with, and prepare to sneak to your target or just take them out outright. This game is built around stealth, so there are numerous ways to go down the stealth path. Choose to sabotage the escape jet seat or poison someone's drink? Your choice. If you don't want to do stealth, that's fine, good luck in advance though xD The bullettime esque mode from Hitman has been cut out, and now it's like a neutered down Witcher Sense. It isn't terrible at the very least, it's actually kind of useful, so I shouldn't complain. Shooting feels alright, the varieties of ways to kill people are pretty good, and I can't think of anything necessarily wrong with it.
GRAPHICS AND PERFORMANCE: Game looks pretty good, ran on Ultra on some settings and it looked fine. Framerate was a stable 60, which is nice. The tutorial level looks kind of dull intentionally, but the Paris level looks great. Remember, though, your luck may vary.
LEVEL DESIGN: The tutorial levels are kind of small on purpose, and you have only a few options. On the Paris level, though, you have a lot more variety and freedom to do what you want.
OTHER STUFF: Right now this is only the first mission and the tutorial. They plan to release the rest of the episodes out gradually, kind of like the Telltale games. I don't really have much of an opinion pro or con to it, personally, though I get both sides of the argument. Also, like I said, performance issues are rampant on other systems, so beware.
FINAL VERDICT: It's only part of a game, yeah. But what we do have is alright. So as of now, 7/10. If you want to wait till the whole game is out, that's fair enough. If not, get the $60 version for the full game. If you're strapped for cash, then maybe the $15, but know that you're going to have to buy the other missions if you do that.

Hitman 2016
I'm not sure why there is all the hate and 'not recommended' reviews about this game. It is awesome. It takes you back to Blood Money style of play, mixed with Absolution technology. Graphics are excellent. The people posting bad reviews about the graphics, obviously haven't cranked up their settings to high/highest. The game really shines and I've loved playing the missions so far. The only gripe I have is that (like the games before) the NPC's are way to twitchy about you - even if you turn away, they will pull a gun on you and then open fire eventually. Returning to form with open ended stealth gameplay, Hitman is the worthy successor to Blood Money fans have been waiting for. There are lots of ways to go about completeing the huge sandbox levels due to a large arsenal of weapons and items, plenty of disguises, and a whole lot of accidents waiting to happen. There's also a few silly hidden secrets for those willing to look for them. That said, the thing that makes this a great game for me is the level of difficulty. There are a number of new systems created to make the game easier for new players, but all of those can be turned off. Doing this combined with going for some of the more difficult challenges makes for a demanding but worthwhile experience.
Replayability has always been a big part of Hitman, and some of the features  from Absolution have been brought over and refined to offer even more. Challenges give more reasons to replay each level, and completing them nets you more weapons and items, different starting locations, and spots where you can recover a smuggled in weapon or item. Contracts is also back, and while the main mode of player created missions still isn't great, the new Escalation Contracts are. Escalation Contracts offers a series of developer created missions that build on each other with more objectives each time. While there is only one set available so far that doesn't take too long to complete, it's still great fun.
The actual gameplay is undoubtedly the best in the series, which is not exactly a surprise since the last good Hitman game was ten years ago at this point. It takes all the basics of Blood Money and improves on them. Along with small tweaks to systems like the AI being smarter and the HUD being slicker, it also just plays better. The shooting, movement, and stealth mechanics all feel modern in a way Blood Money doesn't anymore. The game I could closest compare it to is MGSV: Ground Zeroes, and while this is not quite as good as that, I'd say it's definitely close.
The one real problem I do have with this game is the PC optimization. I have a GTX 980 and I still had to knock it down to medium to get an acceptable framerate. Graphics don't matter too much to me though, so I don't see that as a dealbreaker. However, due to the offline mode missing the progession system, challenges, and Contracts; this game might not be for you if you don't have a stable internet connection. It's also episodic, so for those who don't like paying up front for an "incomplete" game you might want to wait. All in all though, I still think it's fantastic.

This game is plagued by Arkham City. The story is great and will keep you entertained for the whole game. It easily has the best writing in all the series, but is still a little comicy. However, the story creates a much deeper characterization of many important characters, something that was definitely needed in these games. The voice acting is great, and you only notice the new cast if you are really listening for it, if not you’ll just here the normal joker and the normal batman, The gameplay is exactly like past games, fast and free flowing, however it does little to improve this, yeah there might be some new gadgets but overall it does not improve on much. The two new enemies add variety which was much needed but it feels lacking. There is still a strong stealth element in the gameplay which is nice, but again it lacks innovation. The graphics make the game look amazing and the PhysX helps to immerse you into the environment, there is also a very good amount of settings for the game. The challenges mode is also fun and leaves much replay ability as you try to string the best combos possible. Multiple locations and characters also make it feel fresh and exciting. Multiplayer is the new edition, the game mode is actually fun and very fast paced. However it is lacking variety and has a very small community. There were some bugs and glitches in the release but I assume that most of them will be fixed soon, however it is still disappointing to see so many glitches, bugs, and crashes. The open world is now much larger but feels empty. Besides the random crime in progress or the side missions there isn't much to do as you glide around. On that note there is plenty of side missions that will keep you entertained much after the story. The new detective mode abilities are awesome but are way too easy as the game basically tells you what to scan next, leaving no challenge. What the game highly improved was the boss fights. The boss fights now challenge a certain aspect of your abilities and makes boss battles more challenging and pleasing when completed, it also helps you too master each certain ability. The main problem with the game is its lack of innovation. It is a polished version on Arkham City, it may be better than it, but it receives lower scores because of its lack of innovation. It’s a great game that did not offer much to the table. As I was writtingthis an update started, hopefully it will fix the issues.

Synopsis:
Oxygen Not Included is not so much a game as it is a logic machine creative engine. You have various resources to manage for your "duplicates" in a procedurally generated world. They're basically your job doers. Each comes with different stats, decor expectations, benefits and downsides that can wreck your early game if you don't pay attention to which disadvantages you're exposing your base to. (Calling out "flatulence" right now as an early game DESTROYER) If that sounds tedious, don't worry. You only start with three and don't directly control any of them. You assign jobs in the area and your little minions complete those jobs ,unless one of their disadvantages keeps them from doing it. Your "goal" from the outset is to keep these duplicates alive, and to research, make machines, and manage your resources... is what I would be saying if it weren't a dirty lie! You certainly have to keep them alive but the main satisfaction (which I would argue is the real point of any game) comes from how efficiently you have set up your base in terms of germ containment oxygen making, power efficiency, heat managment, and food growing (Along with other minor things that any one of which can royally screw your game over if you completely ignore it). The more self sufficient your base, the more time your duplicates can spend on expanding your base, research, food growing, and resource collection.
Strategy:
A game like this pretty much lives or dies off of you figuring it out, from interface to strategy development, so it'd be a♥♥♥♥♥♥move to the game developers to give away a winning strategy and a middle finger to you for giving away the answer without letting you figure it out for yourself. That being said, I think a few things should be shared for people just picking up the game as early game had poor conveyance to me as to what I was supposed to do. SO:
1) Once you're in game don't worry about any interface button except for "dig". It's the only one that does anything at the time.
2) This game is about resource management, so be sure to check for any menus within menus for important data because this game's interface is more information heavy than an IRS excel document.
3) Some oxygen is actually included.
Pros
- Fun "Don't Starve" aesthetic
- Satisfying gameplay once you get used to the interface
- Addictive in that, "Okay here's how I messed up, here's how I'll solve it next time" kinda way
- Recommended for anyone who spent a lot of their time in vanilla minecraft making logic machines to do crazy stuff that makes it seem like you modded the crap out of it
Cons
- RRRREEEEALLY steep learning curve with no tutorial. Basically press buttons until something happens
- Short game (You could probably get to end game within 30 in game cycles)
- Once you've figured out the mechanics and how to best apply the researched machines, there's really not much to do but expand your base, which is basically just "repeating Steps 1- x"
- Not recommended for when you want to turn your brain off and listen to a podcast as you play
For what it is, and especially as early access, this game is pretty good. I'll admit I'm not too familiar with logic machine creative engines and as basically my introduction to them, I have to say this was an extremely satisfying, so my final rating for the game:
7/10 Play it!

My favorite games are simulation and this one truly delivers. This one is all about building system that will help your people survive. The game doesn't hold your hand while you build these systems either. This means a decent learning curve but a rewarding one. It also means any system and your base feels like your own. I look at other people’s bases and it truly has a different feel then my end. A lot of this I didn’t realize till I played for myself.  Add to it that there are multiply viable ways of solving problems IE producing O2, filtering water, etc. So you are solving problems your way, not the way the developers want you to.
Each new base feels like an excuse to try things differently, more efficiently or completely different build order. With a few hundred hours into this game I can get all the systems I need to survive and easily get to late games. (500+ cycles) At that point it often gets boring since I find myself just amazing more water and unneeded resources.  Yet that is usually a good excuse to wait for next update and/or start a new base and try something new.  That’s not to say the game is too easy with experience. A few too many early stupid mistakes and the base is doomed. Plus I’m confident the late game boredom will be resolved with more content.
The game is not without its issues. Late game it can feel like it takes a while for your people to complete tasks. Since they are busy maintaining other systems, or they just have further to travel. Having more people can help with this a lot. Yet a base with more people is a larger challenge. The AI can make some pretty stupid moves and get them killed/trapped. Yet keeping an eye on them while they build/dig stuff goes a long way. As well as giving them orders in phases. Most weird bugs can be resolved with a save and load of the game.
Ultimately if you are considering get this game you should go ahead and get it. Low risk, high reward from this one.

Starpoint Gemini 2 is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ offspring of the X series and freelancer. From X, it got a lot of different gameplay options, a rich, large world, customization... And from freelancer it got the fast paced gameplay, the great combats, a little arcadey feeling that doesn't interfere with the simulation aspect...
A truly great game.

SHORT: If you want to paly space arcade which is quite easy and has kinda little for you to do (you like to do same thing over and over), then this game is for you. If you want to play space sim that is more difficult and real, play evochron mercenary or some X series (Id prefer evochron, X in my view is much shallower than most of the people would tell).
*********************************************
LONG: ok i waited for some sale for this game for quite some time now as I am a huge space games fan. So when the price went down I went ahead and bought it. Its not a bad game, it just feels... unfinished. My points below:
QUEST LINE - is kinda ok. I got lost time to time in who is who, but its not hard to follow if you pay attention. Not super enganging tough. If you think about cutscenes, forget it. Youl get just some mediocre voice acting and thats it.
SIDE MISSIONS - they are insanely repetitive. There are even no variations on given mission type what so ever. Example - all science misions are about go somwhere, scan something in like 10 seconds and thats it. It does not matter if the diff level is 1 or 40, its always the same (and you can of course do level 40 mission at level 1)... that applies to all non combat missions. Why? I have no idea. Its important to mention that there are like 5 or 6 mission types. And if you think that would not bother you think again, I tought the same... it will.
COMBAT: is the only fun thing and even then its really easy to master. If you are careful, you cannot die in this game. If you do, you just did not get the mechanics right cause once you do, you cannot die. Or you got cocky. You either obliterate anything or run away, which is super easy. Just get some higher level railguns and kill everything. But its fun, really... first game I had a feeling of controlling a big ship all by myself.
On the other hand theres not really extensive tactics to apply. You can either fire manually (which is impossible as theres no targeting computer... and try to hit 1px big thing floating in space) or auto fire without possibility of selecting a priority target.
ECONOMICS: well this is where the whole game sort of breaks down. Theres only one meaningful way to make money - boarding ships and selling them. Really, theres no point in doing anything else for money making, its just not worth the invested time. Doing missions? Hell no, you will get 10x more money from single low level boarded vessel than from any low level mission (and it takes like 1/10 time). Trading or mining? Nah, too much time spent. Hunting for bounties? Even more time spent.
One example for all - at level 1 you are able to board basic gunships. Each sell for 30-120K depenging on its liadout. Side mission on the first levels give you around 10k. So why the hell would you wanna do them except when you need to level up?
At the end of the day you will do just these things in this game:
1. hang around enemy territory near friendly station and board anything you can board (its not hard, just basic math + some upgrades). After you save enough money, go leveling.
2. do side missions just for XP (power leveling, not fun at all) to get to next rank
3. byu new ship, repeat step 1
4. at any given time do the main quest (because why not)
You could do more, but the thing is - why would you? And dont go all out on me with role playing... thats human nature - doing the most effective things to achieve a goal. I dont see why should I go mining if I can make much more money much more easily with much less time spent.
ARMAMENT
is unbalanced. Actually theres no level requirement for any equipment/upgrades/weapons, just for ships. So its very easy to go OP, cause you never have money problem (boarding) so you can buy the best stuff there is straight on. Of course you dont put max level weapons on the basic gunship because of energy consumption, but you get the idea.
Also theres not much to upgrade. I got to the point where at level 35 (out of 60!) I had the best ship (frankly why are we allowed to have the best ship at half of level cap?), everything maxed out (best weapons, most expensive upgrades). At that point you can do only one thing that can influnece your ship and that is blueprint hunting. And that is random. totally random. You just have to do all the stuff over and over and over again and wait for a drop (which is not that often). Not fun at all. And you dont need it, you can be OP even without blueprint equip.
Also its all transferrable to your new ship so once you upgraded let's say engine to the max, you never change it... even if you do this at level 5, you will stay with that upgrade until level 60.
Last thing - only three weapon types + rockets (which are useless) :(
ABILITIES
They work fine, but they are not super essential. You can win most of the fights without using any active abilites. Passive abilities are helpful.
But its nothing extensive, you basically have 4 active abilities that you upgrade (each with sever sub categories but you usually stick to one or two of them). You get a point each level or so. Passive abilities you can upgrade only once per rank, they have quite nice bonuses to make you even more OP (OP square?).
CONCLUSION
This game feels like bugless beta. There is whole level of depth missing and it feels like the devs just put some stuff together not really thinking about how its gonna work together. The boarding mechanics I find the most troubling as it influences all other aspects of the game, its uper easy and makes you do nothing more than that.
It would take some changes to make this game great:
- balancing the money incomes to support role playing (again why the hell would I be a miner?)
- break down the upgrades to more levels and introduce level requirement for better equip
- make different pieces of shields, energy source, engines etc so theres more variety. Right now you only upgrade, but dont replace anything.
- make the side missions more interesting and incorporated into the mechanics (e.g. scanning higher level anomalies would need you to go to enemy territory/needs special equipment/whatever + you would need this to unlock upgrades for some of your equipment)
- more complex tactics
I really tried to like this game as my record shows, but after this time I just totally lost interest in playing. Maybe I did not figure out some of the stuff I did criticise so in that case let me know. But from my perspective you should not buy this game for full price, $10 tops. It gets old very fast.

Ever since I played Starpoint Gemini, I have been a big fan. The original game was very easy ot use and not too overly complicated to use. The game was in 3D, but only flew in 2D, so it wasn't hard to get form point "A" to point "B" with little effort.
Starpoint Gemini 2 takes the original game several steps fruther. The concept is sitll the same. You are a space pilot looking to make a name for yourself in the age of space trader. You can either play in campiagn or in freemode.
Some of the things that have improved since the first game are as follows...
1.) Flight is now in 3D instead of 2D
2.) You no longer have to use jump gates to get to your destination
3.) A lot more ships to choose from
4.) Ships have a lot more upgrades to choose from
5.) Some ships offer a "Flight Deck" where you can send small fighters out while you battle
6.) Not only can you have a flight deck, but you can also choose which kind of fighters you want
7.) This time, you can also land on planets as well as star bases
8.) Combat is lot more "tactical" than before
9.) You can now make friends and enemies, this determines if you are able to land on stations or planets
10.) There are now factions, each with their own likes and dislikes about you and other factions
11.) More items to buy and trade
12.) Major improvementts on comba, flight, and trading system
13.) There is now a fully viewable starchart you can use to determine where you are versus where you go
Overall a much more enjoyable game with added features that allow a lot mroe to do as well as a lot more offer. The added bonus of flight decks is also very helpful for when you need that added help durig combat. If you are into the Space Trader system that has true 3D concept of space flight, this is a good game to get. If you loved Starpoint Gemini, you will love this second part. The added benefit of landing on planets is a major bonus from the original game.

Still too many bugs to be considered a full release. Also there is no real 'story' you pretty much just aimlessly fly around space killing and capturing enemy ships with no real direction or mission. The missions that are there are no more deep than 'kill this' or 'fly here'. This game could be awesome, but gets so close and then falls flat. There is also a really lack of sound effects other than the same repitious laser blast sound 1000 times.

Undertale, the storm of the internet. What can you say that has not been already said?
Story: 7/10
The story is not really anything epic. You are given a bit of backstory in the intro, but in the end story goes along the lines of "You are human, you fall where monsters live and try to get back to surface". It has some depth in it built up in the later portions of the game. It's not bad, and it works, so I can't really say anything else than it might have played it a bit safe on the beginning department.
Gameplay: 9/10
This is the Undertale's bread and butter. After all, this is a RPG where you don't have to kill anybody. Or kill everything. This is done in RPG-style battle menu with options to fight, interact with enemies, use items and spare enemies or escape. When the enemies attack, you move your soul (represented by a heart) in a restricted area to avoid the attacks. This gives you a chance to avoid every single attack you may face and never worry about your health recovery, if you play well enough. Some characters even mix things up and change properties of your soul, making the gameplay even more interesting.
Music: 9/10
Here we go... The music of Undertale is amazing in every way possible. The songs give you so many different feelings, and you basically can hear the dedication of Toby Fox when he composed the music. Every area has a song that nails the feeling of the area, and the subtle changes in the songs at different runs makes the music seem alive, for the lack of better word. There are some songs that didn't quite catch up to better themes of the game, but you can't win in every aspect, right?
Graphics: 9/10
Can't judge, the pixel graphics do the game justice. Sure, they may seem lacking in the overworld, but when battles start, you can see the details of the characters. The pixel graphics and the level of detail in the characters give sort of unique feeling to the game.
Characters: 6/10
My only negativity of the game, and only partially at that. Sure, you can't say anything about our silent protagonist, but sometimes it feels like some NPCs and enemy characters get more character development than others. There are some really weird and different characters, who you may like no matter what, but my slight complaint is that I found about 50% of the characters REALLY annoying. And I felt like they didn't get that much character development, so you couldn't see if they would get better. Maybe that was choice of the creator, but it did put me off a bit.
Overall: 8/10
Undertale is simple, small and short RPG with much good going on. The replay value is insane, the short time it takes to finish a run and multiple endings really make you want to play this game again. Not everyone can like it, but if you want to find something new, small and unique to play, I suggest you give this game a go.

Why I bought it:
I just got this game a few weeks back and honestly, first going into it I was not too enthusiastic about playing. I had seen how much attention this game received when it first came out as well as the huge fan base. Videos and fanart flooded all of my favorite websites and social media, I had friends at school and online discussing this. It was pretty annoying, so I decided to finally buy it and see what all the hype was about.
Why I liked it:
The story is good and the characters are lovable, of course. The fact that you have the options to fight, act, and spare/flee is really cool imo. I'm used to games that don't permit this wide array of choices when playing. The fact that for every new game you make, you get a different FUN level is really cool because it does help to keep the game interesting and funny, something I can really appreciate.
What could've been different:
I avoided all videos and fanart and discussion on this game, so when I played it, I did a neutral run and honestly I kinda wish that the game made more clear that things are more interesting when you complete the game either killing nothing or killing absolutely everything. I also would have appreciated the option to skip entire conversations with people because once you've played multiple times, the dialogue is repetitive and can get boring fast. The gameplay is also a little repetitive. When going through the core, an option to ignore Alphys would have been cool. When playing through the first time, the little notifications are cute and funny and interesting, Alphys is a quirky, insecure, and nice character. But once you've played through, as previously stated, it gets boring and annoying, mainly because her status updates make you stop walking and it feels like you're being slowed down.
How I've played:
My first run was gone into blindly and a neutral route. Tbh I killed Toriel because I assumed that beating her wouldn't mean killing her; I guess I was stupid haha. I spared Papyrus, but killed most everyone else, if not fleeing the battles when my HP was low. I never reset. I played 2 pacifist runs after my first run. I have yet to do a genocide run.

I have spent....waaaaay to much time just...watching.  Not even doing anyathing.  I tried to tell myself I was doing something, but....I was just watching the prisoners go about their daily tasks.  It's incredibly addictive.  Oh, I just need to make sure that my regime change is effective, or I'm getting new prisoners I'm gonna make sure they adapt ok...and so on.
You can play on sandbox mode for infinite money, or play in "regular" mode where money management is quite important.  There are options to generate forests, lakes, and derelict buildings if you so choose.
This is a game that also requires looooaddds of planning and forthought.  While money management is important, its fairly easy to stay in the black, just not easy to have lots of money to spare.  the real strategy comes down to HOW you build the prison.  If you put the canteen to far away from the prison cells and the prisoners spend half an hour walking to the canteen, then they won't have enough time to eat.  And a hungry prisoner is a prisoner that is shivving everyone.  Plus, contraband can be easily brought around an unplanned prison.  If you have a large open area next to your outside wall that prisoners can access, cigs, phones, weapons, drugs, alochol, and more will get thrown over the wall to them.  They will steal from offices, kitchens, workshops, cleaning cupboards, and everything in between.  There's even a crude (for the moment) electrical wiring system to create doors that open on timers so you can automate your prison more.
Oh, and for the love of all that is good and holy....NEVER.  LET.  THE POWER.  DIE.  I learned that the hard way...."Let's see, a metal detector here, and here annnndddd that should be good."  *fast forward to when the items are installed*  *Mechanical Grindy Noise* "THE CRAP HAPPENED TO MY POWER"  *prisoners riot 'cause they like light and ac and hot food*  GG!  New prison...
I highly recommend this game, and even though it can get a bit old after you've fully fleshed out your fist couple of prisons, there always  a new update comes out every month, whether it's a new mechanic, such as gangs, or a new room, such as the mail room.  There are quite a few mods too and a great community that is always making new prisons to check out.

An honest open letter to the negative reviewers of Yooka Laylee,
Hi! I am calling out to the common sense of gamers far and wide on the relentlessly scathing reviews on this glorious game. The devs are industry professionals that have poured their hearts and souls into this project. If nothing else that should be acknowledged regardless of your opinion of them in the recent PR stuff regarding JonTron and Refunds. As of this post, I am nearly 9 hours into the game and have been blown away by how faithful they were to the genre.
But back on track, I'd like to address some of the major topics you guys have brought up. While I am by no means an expert on the topic and do not claim to be, I hope to shine a realistic light on these "issues".
To those claiming the camera is too clunky/moody. I BEG the question, have you ever played an N64-era platformer? Because as someone who played through all of Banjo-Kazooie in preparation for YL, I can attest that this set-up is pretty spot on when compared to BK/BT. Because in all honesty, the devs said from the get-go that they were going to "...create a spiritual successor to our most cherished work from the past!" (
) Which to my understanding means making an N64-esque game for the modern consoles.
To those claiming the level design is incoherent. I would like to bring to your attention that this is a staple of the genre, get over it. There is no getting around that. Platformer levels are all over the place because you are supposed to WANT to explore every nook and cranny.
To those claiming the "voices" are annoying. Really? These are same devs that pretty much coined the gibberish SFX and text thing and you are put off by that? Come on people...
To those claiming the game has performance issues. Yes, it has bugs. This is, put simply, the result of one simple fact. This game was  NOT made by a AAA company. Say it with me, this game was  NOT made by a AAA company. While yes, the Kickstarter was immensely successful, QA is simply not a problem you can throw money at and just magically get a bug-free game. This situation is unavoidable for a team of this size, period, end of story.
To those claiming the game is dated. You are absolutely, 100%, without a shadow of a doubt, correct. And that was completely the point. If you don't like that you should have read the headline of the game description a little closer. Sorry.
The real headline that everyone seems to be missing is that these guys faithfully brought back a genre that had one foot in the grave. All of these "issues" come with the package. Get over it and enjoy this beautifully flawed game, or continue to gripe. Either way, no one who shares my point of view will care if you keep griping, they'll be too busy enjoying the game.
Sincerely,
Galbjorn
P.S. To any devs that manage to end up seeing this, you have my heartfelt thanks and gratitude.

A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away.... I played this gem. Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy is probably, by far, my most favorite Star Wars game.
PS: Despite my gametime is only 3 odd hours or so, I've actually beaten this game multiple times in the past.. with my now abandoned Windows XP machine. Ha.
This game offers two modes, single player where you progress through the storyline as Jaden or Multiplayer where you play against other players in Royal Rumble FFA or Capture the Flag (my favorite mode). This review emphasizes on SP side.
In single player, you'll have to beat three chapters consisting five episodes each to the total of fifteen. And later you have to beat 'boss levels' after each chapter, so make it eighteen. Gametime as a whole for SP mode isn't that long, ten odd hours or less. But still, entertaining. Each episode has its own unique objective, ranging from rescue mission to dismantling bombs. The variety of environment design and levels also make it enjoyable to progress through this single player missions.
Everytime you enter an episode, except boss levels, you'll have a chance to assign one Force Power to pick one among eight options, four Light Core and four Dark Cores. This makes things a bit more personal and customizable to suit your liking. You want to be the real Protector Jedi? Pick Light Cores. Or you want to be the real dark side? Get Rage and Lightning Force for all chaos you want! Do note that picking Cores doesn't affect the ending, despite Luke's review after each Act finished. The ending (good side or dark side) will be affected much later in the game by making a choice. I won't spoil that, though, here.
Customization extends a bit more, where you can select from pre-made character designs and your lightsaber hilts / color. Much later in the game, you'll be allowed to construct more advanced lightsaber like Duals and Staff. And yeah, unlike in previous title Outcast, you'll have this lightsaber right off the bat in your arsenal. Only the Advanced Lightsabers that won't be available straight from the start.
Control mappings admittedly are very nice. You'll have no issue assigning keyboard buttons to specific action e.g Jumping or Crouching. The  menu also can detect modern Keyboards/Mice weird buttons so you can assign the commands to those as well.
Game mechanic is terrific and personally for me it's this game's strongest point. With Lightsaber available in many styles, you can have fun fighting your opponents - slashing right and left and launching Lightning attacks at them. All done in real time! There are few combos you can learn from in-game manuals so that you can have easier fights especially when playing on higher difficulty levels. I rarely trigger my guns, except when forced in one level - in that level your Lightsaber is confiscated so yeah....
Graphic wise, the game's not aged well. In order to 'play' the game properly, you have to get some settings right. First, the tame has to be manually set up if you want to play on widescreens - pretty much modern LCDs. Lower textures are seen from the get-go everywhere - by today's standard, anyway.  There's a workaround for that, though. Mods for textures are also available to make it more bearable if you can't stand the original. Game also refuses to be minimized, making it silly if you love to alt-tab while playing like me.
As it stands, there are game breaking bugs. I've personally encountered bugs where a door essential to progress refused to open (dismantling the bombs mission in a reactor). I restarted that mission from the scratch and hoped to progress, luckily I was able to after restart. Don't expect a patch for this.
However, being an old game, you can expect your weak rig that can't run Evolve or some other high demanding games NOW launches this game with ease, with all graphic settings maxed. Game also is compatible with modern OS, much to my surprise. I am running this game well on Windows 7 x64 and 8.1 x64 without issues - other than issues from the game itself (game breaking bug I wrote above). I can't say about MAC version as I don't have MAC, or Linux if you want to WINE this.
All in all, a very recommended game even for just Single Player if you can't stand Multiplayer.
Old school score: 9.5/10

Returning to form with open ended stealth gameplay, Hitman is the worthy successor to Blood Money fans have been waiting for. There are lots of ways to go about completeing the huge sandbox levels due to a large arsenal of weapons and items, plenty of disguises, and a whole lot of accidents waiting to happen. There's also a few silly hidden secrets for those willing to look for them. That said, the thing that makes this a great game for me is the level of difficulty. There are a number of new systems created to make the game easier for new players, but all of those can be turned off. Doing this combined with going for some of the more difficult challenges makes for a demanding but worthwhile experience.
Replayability has always been a big part of Hitman, and some of the features  from Absolution have been brought over and refined to offer even more. Challenges give more reasons to replay each level, and completing them nets you more weapons and items, different starting locations, and spots where you can recover a smuggled in weapon or item. Contracts is also back, and while the main mode of player created missions still isn't great, the new Escalation Contracts are. Escalation Contracts offers a series of developer created missions that build on each other with more objectives each time. While there is only one set available so far that doesn't take too long to complete, it's still great fun.
The actual gameplay is undoubtedly the best in the series, which is not exactly a surprise since the last good Hitman game was ten years ago at this point. It takes all the basics of Blood Money and improves on them. Along with small tweaks to systems like the AI being smarter and the HUD being slicker, it also just plays better. The shooting, movement, and stealth mechanics all feel modern in a way Blood Money doesn't anymore. The game I could closest compare it to is MGSV: Ground Zeroes, and while this is not quite as good as that, I'd say it's definitely close.
The one real problem I do have with this game is the PC optimization. I have a GTX 980 and I still had to knock it down to medium to get an acceptable framerate. Graphics don't matter too much to me though, so I don't see that as a dealbreaker. However, due to the offline mode missing the progession system, challenges, and Contracts; this game might not be for you if you don't have a stable internet connection. It's also episodic, so for those who don't like paying up front for an "incomplete" game you might want to wait. All in all though, I still think it's fantastic.

Obviously buy the intro pack first to see if you like the game. It's better to commit and potentially waste $15 than $60, even though it will cost more should you decide to buy the full upgrade later. That being said, there's not a lot of content to justify the full purchase right now but the prologue and Paris missions gave me enough entertainment to justify spending $15.
Performance issues need to be addressed, but the game is still very playable for me on older mid-range hardware (i5 4670 and GTX 760). I will definitely give the Paris content another few playthroughs to mix things up.
While I probably won't buy the full game for a while, I did enjoy the $15 intro pack as a good weekend game.
Also, I happen to live in an area with stable high-speed internet. If you don't, don't buy this (at least don't go all-in and buy the full game).

Oh Hitman, the memories this series brings me. I remember back in the day when Hitman: Codename 47 got released, played it at a friends house at first then decided to get it myself, I was 12 at the time, and my step-father at the time diden't really like what I was playing, so he decied to choke me like our bald hero does when I was playing it, just to show me what I was actually playing, good times.
Then came Blood Money and I couldn't stop playing that title, the replay value was immense. Playing the Casino over and over again just messing about with how to kill the targets, kill every single person on the map etc. The Suitcase with the wonderful sniper rifle inside getting past metal detectors and going stone-cold killer mode inside the Whitehouse. And killing rednecks at a wedding. The good times I've had with this title, the memories, what defines Hitman to me is what I had in Blood Money.
Now come HITMAN, and it's like I'm walking down memory lane again to those Blood Money days. And it's only alot better this time around.
First of all, I've turned off every single help/HUD option there is, this makes the game alot more better, you have to think for yourself, actually listen and observe and makes the whole game alot more enjoyable and hard, like it should be. Killing high profiles ain't an easy job, and that's just how I like it.

Opportunities, there are some many opportunities to basically do whatever you want when it comes to killing your targets, I'm 15 hours in (as of this writing) and I'm still finding new and fun ways to take out my targets. The scenery is amazing, it feels soo alive and breathing and adds to the atmosphere of the game really well. The Paris map is huge, alot of areas to discover and find new pathways to your objective. How the AI's react to what you're doing is really great aswell, although they can feel quite stupid sometimes, they feel like the AI in Blood Money, only alittle better. The Challenges they have are excellent. Look at a challenge that looks interessting and start planing on how you gonna do it, adds alot to the replay value.
And that is what the Hitman games really are about, replay value, and this has it. Sure we only have one stage at this moment, but we knew that already, HITMAN is going to be episodic and I'm fine with that. Because seeing how good this one stage is, I can't wait for the next one and the ones after that.
My only complain I have so far is one thing I miss from Blood Money, and its the casual holding of larger weapons in your arm when they're holstered, right now you have them on your back and AI guards do too. Looks so wrong and I really hope they add it in the future. Also, lack of briefcase.

Amazing. Honestly, there is barely anything I dislike about the game, the characters are well-crafted with many layers to them, the story is complex while still being well explained, the humour is perfect and mostly due to good writing instead of sheer randomness. Character backstories can get incredibly detailed, and there are tons of twists in your expectations. The music is ridiculously good, using leitmotifs to evoke nostalgia etc. This game can have you laughing one minute then crying the next. It's also extremely good at making you feel bad for your actions, especially if you choice to go down a *certain* route. It also loves to mess around with it's software, from characters accusing you of running away if you close the game during a fight, to shaking the window, changing the window name, even shutting itself off once or twice.
Gameplay is pretty decent, bosses are challenging with a good difficulty curve, and the game does a great job introducing new mechanics except for with one fight. Think bullet hell mixed with turn-based and throw in a sparing system and that's pretty much it. There are quite a few witty moments with the mechanics of things, that I really can't help but mention, but be wary that there are minor spoilers for the rest of the paragraph. A certain character completely abuses the system, attacking you in the menus and attempting to beat you by doing nothing and keeping it his turn forever. Other characters can destroy options, like the ability to spare.
Graphics-wise, i'm not giving it a free pass just because I love the game. The first area looks bland, and minor enemy models aren't as detailed or polished as other areas. But once you leave this area, it does improve. The second area isn't as bad, and fits the theme of the area quite well. The third area has some really beautiful areas, and the fourth is very detailed. The overworld sprites for characters can't canvey emotion, but this is solved through the use of the battle sprite heads in the textboxes. Overall, I think it looks fine after the first area and it didn't personally bother me at all.
I would say tons more, especially on the character and story side, but I wouldn't want to spoil this game for anyone. Small things about how the game works can be really important to not know about before you need to :)

I sort of wish there was an in between for the review options. This game is pretty decent, but has a lot of issues.
First and foremost for me was issues with getting the game to start. When I first downloaded the game it would not start at all. Updating my device drivers fixed this. Two days later the game would not start at all again. This issue led to having to uninstall the game and reinstall it (which for a game this big sucks). After reinstalling I had even more issues with the game opening in fullscreen but tabbed out. Clicking the game would tab the game in, auto adjust display then tab out again. To fix this I literally had to change the fullscreen settings by editing the settings file.
After all the issues with just getting the game to run, which many people who aren't me won't even run into, there's still some issues I have with the gameplay. The game is fun for the first few hours. Taking down the first couple forts and convoys is fun. But the issue is after the first few times there isn't much more to it. The game falls for many of the "open world action games" tropes like locations that get you high so you can see whats around, taking down enemy bases, and destroy small objects scattered around. A lot of games have done this before, just not with the dieselpunk backdrop of Mad Max.
Ultimately I would recommend getting this game while it is on sale for less than twenty bucks (steam summer and winter sales will probably get it that low, also check humble bundle store) If you're a fan of the Mad Max universe this game is worth at least some of your time. If you like open world action games and think the Mad Max world might make an interesting one then this game is definitely worth your time.

ETS2 Review
This game is flippin' fantastic. I've been playing it a few years now and have seen it go from strength to strength. It appeals to a wide age range. The game really stepped out from the normal boring type of driving games, (including other truck games), mainly because of its modability. The modders help to really keep this game alive, along with (Twitch.tv) video streamers like Squirrel (solo driving mainly), & Eliximus and Eazy_Rider whom I am often in the company of, and drive with in their convoys in multiplayer!
I have several solo profiles in this game where I am maxed out with garages and drivers. My tips for those new to this game would be only to get your first garage driving in solo mode; (you cannot avoid that anyway), and develop that to its maximum five drivers with trucks. That's a workforce of only four other drivers and yourself!
Then when you buy other garages, try to keep them spaced evenly out over the map and only keep them at three drivers! If you expand your other garages to five drivers each, (a large garage), you will find that when you have lots of garages much later in the game that you will not be able to find drivers to man all the expanded positions.
This costs you extra expenses for having garage slots without trucks or drivers in them. (Of course it won't matter financially at some point, because you will end up with more money than god, when you can no longer buy any more garages or hire any more drivers).  It’s not unusual to find drivers like me in the game with many hundreds of millions in the game. e.g. 990,660,330 Euros / $
When I hit that point, I expanded my garages to large ones anyway and used those extra truck spaces to keep a collection of trucks to drive just for myself.
There is nothing left to buy that you cannot afford to just throw-it in a ditch when you are finished with it, without a care to what it cost you.  I wish you could give trucks and money to other people, friends etc to help them get started! (Especially if they have just lost all their game saves and have to start again as one of my family / friends recently did).
MP -You really need to start in solo mode, then you can take that game into multiplayer.  The multiplayer version is a mod that uses an older version of the game.  The MP modders do a great job of keeping as up to date as possible with the most recent release and patch of ETS2 but you must realise that the base game has to be there in the first place in order to mod it! That's why they will always be a version or two behind the main single player game.
There are no AI drivers in the multiplayer version. If you have the latest version of the game, you often have to roll back to make MP (Multiplayer) work. You can get the MP version at ETS2MP(dot com). Tip- make sure you double check which side of the road you are supposed to be on when switching between the UK and the rest of Europe!
If you switch between MP and SP games you might damage your game save - or it becomes unmatchable in the other versions, just try to keep a backup - I name a save game with date, level and type, e.g, ( 2015-12-16 Lev 51 MP ) Then I don't always lose everything completely.
In one profile I did recently lose 10 million and dropped a level or so due to incompatibility issues. (I drove too long and far in SP mode with map mods and different modded trucks and trailers), If only I had made a save at base HQ without the mods, that might have held fast. But you never really know until you try it.
Its best if you have several different profiles that you develop and keep one for the standard single player game, another separate game (or two) for playing with mods. (Sometimes a map mod once used and driven, can never be removed and I still have ghost garages that I bought whilst in a mod map, sitting in my standard SP game). Then finally, perhaps have at least one separate save game for your MP game.  If you already have one SP gamesave at a high level, make some saves off that, (just call them different relative save names), then use those game saves when you go into MP - or want to add mods.
Final Tip - Keep the shiny-side-up and the dirty-side-down!

Started out strong, but falls on its face.
At first I was taken in by the graphics and combat.  But hours into the game I was bored by the repetiveness.
At a few points in the story I was simply too weak to continue, so I had to grind money to get the next better ship.  To do this you can trade/mine/missions/capture ships.  Sounds cool right? Not really.  Mining is terribly boring, if you mined in Eve Online you will hate this very badly.

Trading is completely pointless due to the limited cargo space of all ships in your current price range.  Trading doesn't make any sense at all until you drop 25m on a freightliner...but at that point that's the most expensive ship in the game...so wtf would you need any more money for?
Capturing ships is the most lucrative by far.  BUT...friendly ships will make this extremely frustrating to complete successully.
So you wind up finding a friendly base that is close to an enemy base.  So you can easily run back and forth capturing ships.  You'll do this over and over and over and over again throughout the game to progress, because there's no other way to make money.  And since capturing ships is basically hit or miss, it becomes a headache and chore.
I made enough money to buy a ship with 250 cargo, but found that mining only made about $70k a run.  But instead I can try and find a Corvette and attempt to capture it for ~$500k.  So the gamble is to try the ship capture.  Sure, by the time I am done capturing a ship I could've made almost that amount with mining, but you would be so bored.
The story isn't engaging, and the voice acting is so terrible, I'm wondering if they just made random office workers do the lines.  I WISH there was a way to skip dialogue because I can read faster than the terrible voice acting.
