This game has a lot of heart and good intentions, but has a lot of implementation issues as of version 1.2.
It seems to be under active development, but the issues I have with it run so deep that it is unlikely they will get fixed. Everything that is not world sim is implemented as cheaply as possible, and to fix all of these issues would never make business sense.
- Tutorals are non-interactive and your first 5-10 minutes of your experience is you being interrupted by annoying dialog boxes with way too many bullet points to read in one go.
- The planets and bases do not feel like places, and are just a UI screen with some static concept art as a wallpaper if you are lucky. There is no docking animation. Space stations don't even rate background art. Hence there is no feeling of exploration.
- The campaign is done entirely via comm chatter and dialog boxes and is incredibly limited. You are not going to meet a character at a bar on a space station. That would need character art, space station art, and space bars for that, which is so far beyond the budget of this game as it is now that it's just never going to happen.
- The UI is not finished yet. I stopped playing because I accidentally removed all of my turrets trying to figure out the interface. The button to put them back on didn't work. The only way to figure out what is going on is to do forum searches, but my game was still corrupted because of UI designs so bad it basically looks like the game is broken. If you are 13 you might have the patience for that, I do not.
- Considering how tiny the budget is, it is way over-priced. This should be $20 tops.
- There are missing sound effects for things (e.g. nothing for tractor beams, picking up scrap, and beam weapon sounds are buggy and have start/stop issues).
+ The core sandbox 3d gameplay and navigation, where they did spend their time, is a gem. I hope they can at least make the game playable so I can try and become a pirate fleet commander one day, albeit not in the game I wish it was.
Even though I am giving it a thumbs down, it's not a very strong thumbs down. I do plan on revisiting the game in 6 months or so to see how it is. Taken on its own terms, with UI and tutorial improvements the game could be quite enjoyable, even if it's more of a limited and unimmersive sort.

Seems unfinished. Tutorials are lacking.
The combat is frustrating. For example, I had to search the wiki, guides and forums for some time to find the answer to a very simple question: how to attack neutral ships. The answer is - you have to attack them with manual fire, because automatic fire (aimed by AI) only works on targets that are already hostile. Which is another problem altogether: it's very hard to aim anything non-stationary with manual fire.
There is no lead reticle, there is no auto-pilot which can help you align with the enemy so you can properly aim. I had to circle a neutral gunship for 10 minutes and was unable to hit it with light weapons, which don't require ammo (though I had a slow-firing, slow-recharging gun, might have been easier with a faster weapon). I had to use my heavy weapon after all, a homing missile, though I could finish my target with one or two shots from the light turret. I could accept the minimal UI assistance if I wasn't in command of a high-tech space ship. It's OK in WWII flight sim, and very much awful in a sci-fi setting.
Maybe this isn't an issue when engaging big ships, but still is frustrating. There was a suggestion to add the lead reticule. It was suggested more than half a year ago, the developer said it's a good idea
. Now the game is out of Early Access for more than 3 months and this is still not implemented.
There are other things which still aren't working. For example, you can't delete completed missions from your quest log despite it having a "Delete" button. The only way to remove those completed quest is to load a savegame. It's not a big deal, but it shows that the game lacks polish. Another example: hitting "Reset" in keybinding menu will reset your graphic options along with the keys.
I haven't played the campaign much. Still, it doesn't hook you very well. It starts as a generic revenge story. And without explaining anything the game wants you to go and collect stupid plot coupons to get any idea about what the hell is going on. In short: boring.
The description on the store page says the game has "tons of RPG depth". I disagree. Having three classes each with just 4 skills, a dozen "perks" (rather dull compared to, say, Fallout perks) is not RPG depth in my book. And there isn't enough social interaction with NPCs for this game to feel like an RPG. Space Rangers 2 resembles an RPG much-much more than Starpoint Gemini 2 (it's also a much better game so try it if you haven't).
The graphics are OK. Nothing impressive. I liked the music in the main menu. That's about all the pros I could find.
All in all Starpoint Gemini 2 is a rather bland Elite/Privateer-like game without any cool features to be excited about. Or maybe I haven't found them yet. One reviewer mentioned the game being an acquired taste.
I try it again after finishing with more worthwhile games I bought at the current sale, but right now it will have to rest. It's my first big miss during this sale.

Wander a vast, bare, yet visually stunning wasteland in your own creation of twisted steel, bare rubber and of course, guzzolene!
I've had this game sitting about for a while, bought in the summer sale as I'd heard some good things about it but haven't been sure exactly what to expect - but I can say now that it's good.
Graphically it is impressive, considering the Mad Max wasteland is a bare and sandy world with some rocks dotted about the game has been designed to quite often make you stop and stare at the horizon and upwards into the extremely picturesque sky. Add that to the characters, vehicles and barrelling infernos that you've just exploded in a classic Mad Max metal on metal fight, and you get quite a good ride.
Gameplay wise, the driving handling is excellent - a very good balance between realistic physics dependant on the terrain and the ability to keep control while smashed and battered between five or more other vehicles with everything around nothing but a blur. On the other side - out and about as Max with clenched fists - the combat is fairly basic and forgiving for the most part while still very entertaining, stringing together hit after hit, counter-attacks and dodging the even crazier weapon-wielding maniacs. Throughout all of it you quickly build up an arsenal of weapons and tools to aid you both on foot and in the seat.
As common with most modern open-world games, there can be a lot of grinding - many camps to gain entry to in order to take over for Max's cause, along with various other structures to ram, harpoon and explode as you roar across the sand, to reduce enemy threat and scavenge the main valuable material to collect - scrap metal. For the most part I find this aspect of the game rather good, I've spent plenty of time putting the story missions on hold to reclaim the barren lands, and this is an example of the general fun to be had with the game as I usually despise the number-crunching find-this take-out-that cooker-cutter aspects of other open-world games (cough-Ubisoft-cough).
Overall I would very much recommend anyone who enjoys the Mad Max franchise to have a go, if anything it is a blast to jump in the seat and roar across the dunes in your very own road warrior machine, hopping in and out at a moments notice.

Mad Max is a hell of a lot of fun. The developers of this game love the Mad Max universe and it shows. The game looks amazing, it's extremely optimized (I'm getting always 60+ FPS at Max settings with no frame dips, at 1440p on my GTX 970 which is amazing), and it plays like a dream.
You play as Max, who has everything taken from him, again and again. After a near fatal encounter with a major boss of the wasteland, you encounter a mechanic who helps you along in your journey to take down the evil factions that control the wasteland while building the ultimate battle vehicle.
In Mad Max you get to customize your own wasteland vehicle named the Magnum Opus. There are tons of upgrades to obtain and ways to customize your vehicle to fit your playstyle. The game world is massive, with tons to explore and enemies to defeat. The car combat is awesome, from the enemy convoys you take on, to taking out enemy vehicles with a shotgun blast to the fuel tank that sends them into a firey explosion. The on foot combat is great too, and well polished.
Overall, I'd reccomend Mad Max. It's a hell of a good time.

An entertaining, brain-teasing, pretty, well made game. I'm not too familiar with the classic Hitman titles, so I cannot compare. I only completed Absolution, and I find this one a better experience, it feels like a puzzle with multiple solutions, and it's fun to try them all. I think it works very well with the episodic release model, because it would leave a player with a single level until a new one is released. Willingly or not, he'll have time to learn the environment and try different approaches. In Absolution I personally was too focused on the story progression, and didn't care for the mechanics of the assasination - and when you rush through a level, you might miss a lot of fun. In this game it's quite different, it feels quite natural to replay the same mission multiple times; you memorise the events and characters, and see them from a different angle each time. Challenges stimulate you to try different approaches, but I wish some of them were not explained, leaving discovery of their meaning to the player (like hidden Steam achievements).
I do not experience any performance issues, I have GTX 960 and an old Phenom II x6 CPU, the game is locked in Low textures, but looks great and gives me an average of 40-50 fps in its benchmark. I switched to Exclusive Fullscreen mode for a smoother experience, and do not notice any lag or stuttering. No bugs either yet, touch wood. Online mode works fine for me, I don't see a problem in being connected while playing. Offline mode worked in beta, I expect it work here as well. So technically I have no complains.
But of course, as usual, most things related to Russia are wrong, sometimes so ridiculous - it's cute. I mean, people calling each other "comrade", privates telling a KGB general to shove off or saying "howdy" instead of saluting, Soviet vodka having a non-existent brand (and furthermore, a word that was invented about 10 years after), Soviet privates wearing sailors' vests... I think it was intended as a joke, really, it couldn't be so ridiculous on purpose. Or could it?..
Well, and if we're really nitpicking - I don't like the protagonist's voice much. The actor is somewhat straining to sound rough and tough, and it sounds cheap, more suited for a teenagers game like Borderlands or Bulletstorm. Agent 47 evidently has high intelligence, he acts with precision and focus - I'd expect him to speak in the same fashion. And his voice should be as unremarkable as his looks - to blend with any disguise. Good thing he doesn't speak much.
But all in all, I enjoy this game. I recommend it to anyone who likes stealth, puzzles and silenced pistols.
Update: I haven't yet played all episodes, I'm in Marocco now, but it seems that each episode is huge and could easily be a separate game. I had a lot of fun in Italy, and going to replay it once I finish the game. With only the episodes I played already it seems like a bargain. Highly recommended!

This game is not only fun but continues to show improvement and potential.  The devs have scheduled updates which is displayed as a countdown timer when you first log in.  This assures players that the game is continuously being worked on and improved upon.  I can't speak for most Alpha's but that's a + in my book.
If you're new to the game You will be doing a lot of strategizing as you start off.  Most players want immediate gratification when playing a game, this is not that kind of game.  It's all about surviving and exploring.  Get to know what does what and how things work.  Don't start off expanding at a fast pace as this can lead to a lot of downfalls for beginners.  Check your surrounds and progress gradually unless you know what you're doing.  There will be trial and errors as you progress but that's a good thing.  Failures can and will happen but you will learn from them which inevitably improves your game play.
The only con I have about the game is the optimization.  As you introduce duplicants and items into the game eventually it will start to slow down.  This usually happens to me once I get past Cycle 250 or higher.  You have 3 different speeds to play from, Normal, Medium & Fast.  You can change game speeds at any time.  I usually play at Fast speed because I know what I'm looking for and what I need to build.  As the game starts to lag in higher cycles I move over to Medium or Normal speed to get back to normal game play.  Having a PC/laptop that runs high end games may help a bit but after a while everyone runs into the same issue.  The game eventually begins to slow down once you've expanded too far and you're working with too much.  I'm sure the devs are aware of the issue and will eventually tackle it.
In the end it may not be for everyone.  If you want to see some gameplay just YouTube ONI and check it out.  You will get an idea of what it's all about.
(Note Added: 11/27/2017): The low FPS drop and lag are getting worse.  This is after I installed the automation update.  It used to be that I wouldn't get low FPS till I reached cycle 250 or higher with 10 or more dupes but now I am getting low FPS after the 4th cycle with only 3 dupes.  I like the game but something needs to be done about this because it's affecting gameplay at the start.

Being an Arkham "ORIGINS" game: it's a prequel! And it both sucks and rules at the same time. The success of the prequel comes from the story aspect where WB Montreal explains how "wuvable B-Man" met around 10-12 of the Batman franchise characters! This will include Deadshot, Jim Gordon, Barbara Gordon (and her secret identity ^^), and some bosses I was really looking forward to, as seen in the trailers: Copperhead and DeathStroke!
The prequel nature of this title debacles in the gameplay aspect since at the start you have more twice the♥♥♥♥♥♥you had in the beginning of Arkham City! This includes the Grappnel Accelerator, among other useful gadgets.
The gameplay is the same as AC (some small tweaks and combat gadgets have been added) which is great! Now animations feel a bit more fluid but Batman feels slightly slower overall. You see, in Arkham City, you could punch a guy so fast he couldn't punch/counter. In Origins combat, while very familiar, feels harder and requires more skill from the player.
You should also be happy to know that the game works perfectly with mouse and keyboard and the PC port is really good!
The graphics are an overall improvement over Arkham City, snow effects are f*cking extraordinary: easily the best I've ever seen! Particle effects are also really fantastic and the punch sounds are beefy and powerful and you feel like a badass!
Like said above, sound design is solid! The enemy's guns sound like guns, specially the freaking snipers which are really annoying since they take around 40% of your health per-shot! Every time you punch a guy you feel like you are going to get your whole arms through the thug's face!
Moving to the story: It's the best of the Arkham franchise! It's well done, it has enough twists and "Holy-sh*t! Awesome!" moments to keep you pumped until the very end, which is satisfying enough (since it's a prequel, the previous 2 games follow the events of this game, so this game's ending isn't a conclusion to the batman games by any stretch of the imagination!).
This game also has cool enough side missions to give you a few more gameplay hours without outright boring you from the beginning! I must highlight the 2 assassin/boss side quests!
Another thing this game pulls off really well are the boss fights! They all feel different, varied and try to put the various gadgets you have to good use!
Origins is also the first Batman Arkham game to have a Multiplayer mode! Is it good? Yeah! The concept is genious and a nice variation over the standard Multiplayer modes. The are 3 teams, 2 of them are standard thugs with guns (the 3rd-person view and handling is surprisingly good! Guns also feel good, surprisingly enough!), the other team is of 2 players (where one is robin and another is batman, and they play nicely, just like in the single player (well, batman that is, you can't play as robin...but he plays exactly like batman but with a bullet shield. He plays just like Batman Arkham City (both the Robin DLC and the Harley Quinn DLC) which is nice!).
The Multiplayer customization is vast and extremely deep, it has packs that you get by completing stuff in the SP campaign and MP challenges and stuff like that. There are many guns and level ups in the thugs! As for Batman and Robin it's isn't as varied and deep, but that was kind of expected...
My biggest problem with the multiplayer is definately the matchmaking system: it's console ported and it doesn't work very well...it never does, anyways...
You will have lag throughout your gameplay sessions but nothing gameplay-breaking! It's perfectly servicable and compared to other bullsh*tty matchmaking games like Aliens: Colonial Marines, Arkham Origins works amazingly well!
Overall the game seems kinda perfect, doesn't it? Yeah, almost: It's launch was a disaster (I've seen worse trainwrecks though!) and right now, it has like a bug or two very far in-between and sometimes enemies will get stuck on the terrain causing you to sometimes break your whole combo chain. But since I'm not a combo-chain junky, I didn't mind that. I was more worried about the questionable geometry overall: sometimes there are very small places where you can be and right at the side, you can't. You can't crouch and pass under a pipe when in some other, narrower places, you can, among other annoying stuff. But this is really far in-between and don't break the experience at all. I never got stuck in terrain or anything like that, which is swell! :D
Overall, what's wrong with this game is: rare but annoyingly low res textures! Mediocre matchmaking system! Anti-climactic bossfights: (Shiva and Deadshot come to mind) and Bane's is repeated like 3 ♥♥♥♥ing times!
Nothing that stops me from recommending it at full retail price of 49,99€ or regional equivalent (I bet Australian pricing is absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t so there you have it..)
-It's easily a 9/10, one of my GOTY nomenees and overall I'd say it beats Arkham City in terms of gameplay, gadgets, boss fights, etc. (well, except the fact that AC was 100% fluid bug-free gameplay and it was highly detailed. Origins is more unpolished than it's predecessor, sadly...)
-So that is it, my review of Origins, I think I'll do Dishonored after this, I've already been vastly asked to so a review on it.

I enjoy the game, but there are too many inconsistencies and problems behind the game to enjoy. Here are those most significant.
-Your base is set to die from the start, meaning, you have to move around and abandon bases as you deplete all resources around you. May be fun for others but I personally like working to turn around and look at the beauty I made instead of a line of pollution and destruction I left behind, only to turn around (facing forward) to see nothing left. What is worse is that you cant simply pack up and go, controlling these mindless buffoons is a near impossiblity. I guess this is symbolic of real life but I really just want to play a game to relax, not to have a timer glued to the side of my head and hearing every tick.
-Materials are still absolutely absurd. Many of the materials make little sense and are still not diverse enough to really feel  "right." Things that are built also feel off and are also restrictive, as in, their function is greatly focused, making there only few ways to tackle problems. I like wide variety to solving issues with different mechanisms and set ups but with this game, cant really do that. Biggest problem is the algae! This really set me off because algae in real life, grows itself and uses water. In this game, apparently, algae cant grow itself and dies off without a constant supply. This defies the fundamental value of growing and reproducing all in one mechanic. Plus how do you extract oxygen from algae in a machine and release it into the environment? The only thing you can extract is triglycerides and lipids for possible biofuel, not oxygen. But ya got to remember, this game is built to have you die, you cant die if you have realism incorporated into the making of these materials.
-Decor. I detest terraria but at least we could build background walls. Encorporate that into the game because having your base sealed, air conditioned, and having nice tile and wall design is worthless if you have pipes, wires, and natural stone as your background wall... just poor asthetics. Makes having a base just feel ugly and unfufilling.
-flora and fauna, they just dont sit right, and I am not talking about in your duplicant's stomach. There is little diversity and they seem to have absolutely random roles in the ecosystem. They dont bring a feeling of a "feasible" ecosystem one would find in another planet. I know this is just a game but it really bugs me. What feeling the flora and fauna bring me is an empty world overall just bland and synthetic. It almost feels like ed edd and eddy where the only characters in the show were the specific kids and when they went to school, no one else, not even teachers... emptiness. Cooking (and this is what really sets me off) is also worthless. Lice plants are the best to grow... no recipes for them but to render them almost inedible. The other recipes are virtually impossible to do and even if you did em, takes a bunch of resources and time to have it eaten in 10 seconds about... fair trade off man, fair trade off, especially when you gotta move in the next month.
-Speaking of bugs, and not those that eat your resources every night until you kill them, the game has a real problem with these. I will order my duplicant to break a tile and replace it with something else, he then randomly gets stuck in the thing he builds, as if he used his head as a material. Then duplicants are initiating different animations for various activities that actually change what role they are initiating, meaning, if they go to bed and the running animation engages, they get no actual sleep and stay running indefinitely until you manually do something. Tons of other bugs, but you get the idea.
-The duplicants. Oh boy, look at all these customized stats! So diverse, so inspired, so calculated. No, the duplicants' stats are randomly generated. Just keep generating until you get the best set up and successfully avoid all unwanted traits. Altogether, half of traits are worthless and 66% of bad traits must be avoided otherwise one will find themselves in bad predicaments. It is like a game that incourages various set ups but when it comes down to it, only a certain set up can win you the game, so you have to trial and error. This game is a Eugenics simulator guys. Assigning roles  and jobs is also infuriorating. They just dont resond correctly and you will see them doing things absolutely wrong, so wrong, it is wrong. Nothing right, just wrong, I find myself so exhausted from screaming at them that it almost feels like playing hey you pikachu... The horror.
Things I like:
-Music is gorgeous, I am in love.                                -Great feeling of new possibilities.
-Model design and animations are stellar.                 -Neat mechanic design of control.
-Interesting ideas that are not executed right yet.   -Difficulties in game that other survival games do not have.
I like the game but come on, put more stuff into this. It needs asthetics, it needs more organic life, it needs more inorganics. In needs more gases, more elements, more materials, more crafting recipes, and it needs better duplicants. If you put in a mechanic of disease, put in a means of properly fighting them off, even if it is boiling water. I feel like I am running off of caveman logic of redirecting my water through hot zones and then cold zones to fight off bacteria instead of just boiling and allowing water to cool with a pot. This game is good I will say that but it can be great, it can be stellar, but it is not. Other people may like it, but I look into its intrinsic qualities and see a face full of emptiness.
This is a very hard game, hard to live for a long time. Overall I would give this a 8.5/10. It is a good game, but even on the easiest difficulty it is hard to survive for more than 100 days.

If you liked Conker's Bad Fur Day, Donkey Kong 64, and/or Banjo-Kazooie/Tooie, you will probably like this game. Don't go into this expecting anything more or less than another N64-era Rare platformer. Nothing about this beyond the graphics and engine is next-gen, so if you're looking for innovation then this is not the game for you.
It's a charming, fun, and light-hearted game. For the hour I played, I felt very happy and relaxed. The characters are funny and strange. The scenery is beautiful. The art direction in general is playful and really fun to look at. I love the soundtrack. It's fun to play.
There are some problems though. The camera is a little janky, and I've had framerate problems (I have a GTX980M and an i7 processor, plus I have G-sync). Also the options menu seems a little sparse - there isn't enough control over some aspects of the game (like turning the character voices down, or lowering the quality of specific graphical elements). Also, don't play this with a keyboard and mouse - use a controller.
I know there's a lot of controversy surrounding this game right now, but I honestly couldn't give less of a♥♥♥♥♥♥about that. It's a fun game, it's worth playing if you want another classic N64-era Rare platformer to play, and... that's about it. You don't always have to reinvent the wheel to create something worth playing.

Unlike the space sims before it (Freelancer) and the modern ones coming out (Elite: Dangerous and Star Citizen) which focus on the mechanics of a more agile fighter, Starpoint Gemini 2 focuses much more on a capitol ship feel. You're not a lone pilot darting through space in a dogfight, you're sitting at the helm of a Carrier, deploying fighters, and watching your crew unload your ship's payload. Power management is stressed, as is the use of powers and items that bolster shields, shut down enemy systems, etc.
One thing I love about this game which I have not yet seen in another space sim is the ability to send your troops over to capture another ship. This happens to be one of the best ways to make money, and is extremely fun.
Unfortunately it doesn't give you any experience (which seems a little peculiar, considering it's an integral part of many people's strategies), but the payout is fantastic.
All in all, worth buying, though I haven't played it since Elite: Dangerous came out lol

Greetings as always!  Let me start by stating that I backed this game on Kickstarter and both play and greatly enjoy the card game.  Overall this game is more or less a tablet version of the card game on PC and it mostly accomplishes this goal.  But, do I recommend it?  No, I do not.  The price is right on this product but even still time has a value and I’d rather be sitting across a friend with the physical cards in hand.
Graphically and audio wise this game does what it sets out to very well with 8bit style graphics and audio.  You get exactly what you’d expect knowing the game and its goal.  The cards look just as they do in physical form and the audio brings up that old school 8bit feel very well, I only wish there was more to the game and there have been several people (myself included) with memory leak errors when running the game.
With that said, mechanically you are getting a game with very little in the way of features.  Simple skirmish level modes with both AI and other players, this game really needs more features to be a PC based game, even for 4.99.  There are so many great modes to play with the core game and even borrowing from other online card games could add a lot of variety.  The game is also annoyingly slow, lacking options to optimize your game experience.   I know it is silly but the AI does seem to have the right card for the right time in most games and I rarely felt I had a game on lockdown and felt like I was playing catch up most games.  This is a silly complaint as I see no reason for this to be intended and is probably confirmation bias showing its ugly face.
To be blunt, this game should have never been on steam, as a table-top gamer I feel this game should have never made it to digital period but it does do a decent job in the world of tablet and phone gaming but still, it should have not been on steam.  The only way I can recommend this game is if you really love Boss Monster but have no friends who want to play the physical version.  Uncompetitive card games are usually poor choices for digital ports as there is a sense of community when playing physically against another player and games like these really need something added to make them worth it.  Love the game, but the port isn’t worth it.

2) the interface for moving your cards around feels clunky.  Espcially the casting as it uses an interupt and it took awhile to figure out how to do that, it could have been a bit tighter. I understand that when you are playing PvP you want to keep clipping along, but in a single player game, it feels a bit forced.
3) the hero portion feels a bit slow, I played on normal speed, and had enough trouble with interupts, so not sure if I would want to bump it up to the next speed.
All and all I think they could have done slightly better even if they charged a bit  more.  The potential is here for a fantastic game.  Should you buy it, I would say if it is on sale, it might be worth a look espeically if you are looking to buy the board game.   My Score is 5.5/10  since it was fun to play and I enoyed the game or two I played, but not sure if it has a long term potential.  If they had a choice of Maybe, I would pick that, but for now I am going with no for a recommended buy.
PS. I have changed my mind, as a single player game it is not so bad, I do wish a few players would wander into the online room... The score remains 5.5/10

Short comment/Kurzkommentar/一言感想
EN/ A successful open world game in the Mad Max universe. To survive, you will steal anything you can need from your enemies, kill them, and if necessary, you will eat maggots of their corps to survive. Law and rules are invalidated in this world. Those who wants to survive, will need a strong Will, and a highly customized car. Shoot on enemy vechicles with rockets (not realy a rocket), fish the enemy driver out of his vechicle with a wired harpune, etc..., there are plenty of ways to finish them off. It will also happen a lot that you will have to fight with your fists. In fact, Max is the good guy in this world, but it feels like that he is the baddest guy around... If you like opne world games with racing elements and a lot of explosions, then Mad Max won't be a bad choice at least.
DE/ Ein gelungenes Open World Spiel im Mad Max Universum. Zum überleben stiehlt Max von seinen Gegnern alles was er so gebrauchen kann, tötet sie, und ggf. isst er Maden aus deren Leichen um zu überleben. Gesetze und Regeln sind in dieser Welt außer Kraft gesetzt. Wer überleben will, braucht einen starken Willen, und ein aufgemotztes Auto. Schieß die gegnerischen Fahrzeuge mit Raketen (ist zwar nicht 100% akkurat) ab, oder angel den gegnerischen Fahrer einfach mit einer Seil-Harpune aus seinem Fahrzeug, oder oder oder, es gibt so viel Möglichkeiten die gegner außer Gefecht zu setzen. Es kommt auch sehr häufig vor dass du mit deinen Fäusten zuschlagen musst. Eigentlich ist Max ja der gute in dieser Welt, aber irgendwie ist er auch der bösartigste.... Wer Open World Spiele mit Rennelementen und vielen Explosionen mag, macht mit Mad Max zumindest nichts falsch.

First and foremost I'd like to point out that, while I clicked "Yes" under the "Do you recommend this game", I do not wholeheartedly recommend anyone to just pick this game up on a whim unless it's on a steep sale (50% or more off), though that's just my opinion.
It seems like the vast majority of the positive reviews for Spec Ops: The Line stem from the story and it's the same for me...though I'm nowhere near as "OMFG this game is God's gift to storytelling in gaming " star-struck as a lot of other reviewers seem to be. It was an interesting and attention grabbing storyline, but nothing that groundbreaking or shocking in terms of the entertainment industry. Don't get me wrong. The guys and gals at Yager certainly pulled no puches when it came to delivering exactly what they set out to in terms of message, with little concern for pandering to potential nay-sayers. I applaud them for that and their efforts produced a somewhat gripping and very gritty look at the more unpleasant aspects of war. They did not, however, produce a flawlessly executed, shocking, in your face experience. There are holes in the narrative's execution that make the "shocking twist" at the game's end pretty obvious...and honestly a little cliched/played out.
Spec Ops starts with you assuming control of Capt. Martin Walker, a Delta operative leading a 3-man team into post-catastophre Dubai on a simple recon mission. And this is where the first little nudge in the storyline pops up. As the team enters Dubai they encounter a group of dead US Soldiers. Upon discovering that some of the bodies are recently deceased, instead of following his directives and radioing the situation to his superiors, Walker tells his team their mission has changed from recon to survivor rescue...with no real reasoning other than "these men were killed recently so there
be other survivors". It might just be me, but that rose a little red flag with me in regards to how this story would play out, just a little one, but one none the less. Later, as your team presses through the ruins of Dubai, you come across
.
It's subtle, so long as the player isn't paying attention (it may even be a slight bug in the game considering Yager's plethora of subtle hints/nudges/clues sprinkled thorughout the story in obscure areas or deftly hidden in plain sight), but it's a big giveaway to the game's ending...provided you can catch it. There are other scenes that have the same effect, so long as the player is quick/quick witted enough to spot them:
.
Having the ending more or less pegged hardly dampened the story for me though. I was hooked the whole way through and thoroughly enjoyed my time with Walker and his team. Unfortunately, their story driven tale is buried within mediocre graphics, subpar gameplay and clunky controls. These gameplay issues are the biggest tempering point for my qualms with the game's $30 price tag. I don't care how good your story is/you think it is, that doesn't give you a free pass to skimp on the fine tuning of the gameplay.
If you're looking for an enjoyable, psychological, story driven game giving you the most bang for your buck...look elsewhere. The story is there, but an observant player can begin picking up on the ending before the halfway point of the game. Plus, it doesn't help that the whole
gimmick has been utlized in much more effective means throughout the gaming and movie industry.
If you're willing to look past the clunky controls, mediocre 3rd person gameplay and lack of any real replay value...and you're willing to drop $30 knowing all of this...then by all means Spec Ops can be an entertaining and charming game.
All-in-all Spec Ops: The Line delivers a potentially enthralling story that unfortunatley finds itself bogged down by lackluster efforts at polishing the overall gameplay. It's an entertaining game if you can overlook its flaws, but would be better served at lower price. I give it a 6.5/10 for the potential the story holds despite the downfalls of...well pretty much every other aspect of the game.

I know that this review may be late in the overall scheme of things, but I'd like to highly recommend this game to anyone who wants to find a game purely for the storyline and doesn't care as much for the mechanics.
Spec Ops: The Line boils down to being a game that ultimately used its mundane 3rd person shooter gameplay to its advantage to cause the player (you) to experience what the horrors of war can be like.
You can read reviews and the plot of this game, but that is nothing compared to actually having to go through all of the decisions you make in the game and witnessing your own actions first hand. For me the turning point where I went from "okay this game is going like I read it to be and I'm not feeling that emotional kicker" to "oh man that was a little too much. I think they should've dialed that back. I feel kinda queasy just thinking about it. This is really absolutely properly depressing" around the halfway mark at which you are at a point of no return. Another thing that I really liked about this game are the multiple choices that you are presented in the game. There is no real right or wrong in the choices you make during the game, but I really appreciate tha the game developers allowed players to think outside the box, as I was able to make decisions opposite to what the game might psychology pressure you into doing (going into detail about what my decisions were to give a better example would unfortunately give major spoilers, but what I do feel comfortable in saying is that essentially you are able to make the more neutral decision in the opportunities the game supplies you so that you can be more merciful or morally on the high ground).
I would like to say though, to ANYONE WHO HAS A HISTORY OF SEIZURE/EPILEPSY/ETC that can be brought on by BRIGHT REPEATEDLY FLASHING LIGHTS THERE IS A SHORT SEGMENT OF THE GAME THAT MIGHT TRIGGER SUCH MEDICAL ISSUES SHOULD YOU HAVE THEM and I would like to warn you of that as I don't recall the game ever warning the player of this during the beginning credits/startup. For anyone else WHO DOES NOT HAVE A HISTORY OF SEIZURE/EPILEPSY/ETC I would like to tell you that in a certain segment of the game *no your graphics card is not crapping itself* (as I personally thought it was when I first got to that level). It is simply put a really clever and creative way to drive home the dive into maddness so don't freak out when it starts happening.
I wish I could write a lengthier review, but I know that whatever I write won'd do any justice for the story of the game, it is simply something you have to experience yourself. The game play is like I said above really mundane and forgettable, and often times can be really annoying (it is a 3rd person shooter but not as refined or easy to control and navigate like Max Payne 3 was to give an idea to anyone with questions. I say this because I had trouble countless times getting into cover and shooting during the game in comparison to other games). While this was often times a source of major complaint and frustration while I played the game, I still really enjoyed the experience simply for that storyline. It is just simply put that powerful.
I bought the game during a Steam sale for what I believe was around $7 and I'd highly recommend this game at that price point. After you play this game you will end up greatly hating yourself as you watch a man spiral into insanity and question not only his decisions, but your own (during those decision opportunities I stated above).

There's no end game goal, it's just a "survive as long as  you can" and I'll tell you a secret, with proper use of the technologies you get, you can survive forever (you're able to create more water than you use, and you can use water to create oxygen).
This game would be cool if there were like a "escape from the planet" type of thing going on. Forcing a person to explore to try to find a way out. Or a way to the surface. Or a way to hell.
Or anything at all to make this interesting. But that's my content complaint.
Mechanic complaint: too few technologies (with obvious winners), gas moves too slowly/gets stuck in weird places (I'm looking at you hydrogen), there's no real, strong way to develop your characters into being meaningful, also, unintuitive gameplay: more people isn't better, but it's made to seem like it is with the way the portal glimmers and shines so seductively.
So, all in all, I would not recommend this game to anyone other than maybe someone I felt like messing with so they'd waste money and be annoyed. The only really interesting part of this game is the plumbing.
And I generally don't play games for plumbing.

This review is based on my first couple of hours in the game.
I backed this game on kickstarter, which means I've had a horse in this race since before betting began. Even with my inherant bias, Yooka-Laylee has too many ridiculous design choices, frustrating hinderances, and unbearable sticking points for me to defend.
From the start, the game feels sluggish and annoying. Not much text can be skipped which, with the game's ludicrously low scroll speed, will leave you waiting for the characters to catch up with your reading.
During the tutorial, I gained the feeling that the moon pool was particularly shallow. I had assumed at the time that the game would unlock each of the abilites in succession in order to tutorialise me on each in order. This, however, was not the case. Instead, moves are drip fed to you throughout the game. This really rubbed me the wrong way, the worlds are filled with things to do, provided you have the right abilities. Without them, the levels feel empty and generally boring.
After aquiring the abilities you are presented with yet another caveat. Every ability uses power and power is a pain to recover. Using the roll ability is genuinely enjoyable. I loved rolling around in the toybox but unfortunately, that's not possible in the actual game. After rolling for a short while you'll run out of power. To get more power, you have to walk towards the nearest buterflies. The butterflies are rather sparse and their hitboxes are tiny. They add several layers of minor frustration that builds up tremendously over time.
The levels themselves are expansive, which wouldn't be a problem if you weren't collecting a bunch of items. Getting every single Quill is just plain annoying. They're scattered across the whole level and often tucked into tiny, unnoticable corners. Collecting all 200 in a level is simply unreasonable.
Yooka-Laylee is definitely not worth the asking price. The gameplay is nothing short of irritating. Each section of the game feels archaic and poorly designed. Playtonic has taken the good out of the classic platformer and served us the bad.

TL;DR - A buggy uncontrollable mess of a game
So I'm going to start this off by saying, it looks fun. I see the trailer, youtubers playing it, so I buy the game. I'd also like to say I am using a keyboard and mouse trying to play this game, because I don't have a controller. Trying to play it, (this is back in December of 2016) the invite button won't work, we can't join lobbies, and we abandon it after 20 minutes. We come back to it the day I'm writing a review, and for 11 months of development, it's not much better.
UI Problems
Trying to start a private lobby, the option to make it private doesn't work, you just spam click it all you want, but it doesn't switch. You have to restart your game to make your customizations on your character show up. Trying to change the settings, I can not bind in-game actions to my mouse. Trying to change the graphics settings, clicking doesn't change it, I try and use the arrow key, and all it does is rotate the 3D menu sideways, making the words tiny yellow lines, the arrow keys don't work for putting it back. And overall, even clicking on the correct text is difficult since it (the selector) likes to bounce around. When in game, you have to spam click in the menu to actually get anything to work, and you can't access settings mid game. The controls also aren't displayed in the input menu, just blank.
Gameplay Problems
Trying to move, every button (WASD) goes forward. Nothing to tell you what the controls are, just throws you into a game and you're expected fo figure out how to move around. WASD started working properly when we were on the fight ring map, (didn't work on blimp, billboard, or shipping containers) and it takes ages to re-direct where you're walking. Sometimes you fall out of the map and aren't killed, sometimes while in-bounds the camera zooms in and cuts you out while still alive, and other times it'll start a round putting every player looking at a brick wall, with no visual of any of the characters.
Overall, it's a peice of crud and I do not at all reccomend this game to anyone for any reason, maybe when 1.0 comes out I'll come back to it, but for now, I'm uninstalling the game.

This game takes on both the FPS genre and RPG and mashes the two together to create something great.
You explore the giant world of Pandora, killing most things in your way. The game is whacky and completely nuts, you will open LOTS and LOTS of containers and everytime you walk up to one, even small ones you will be excited for what is inside it - even though it is probably just some ammo. Even though the game is nuts the charactars themselves are great, along with the plot. You will find yourself laughing at the stupidity of the game one moment then being drawn into the plot the next. Handsome Jack, the villian of the story is a great villian, he is crazy and hateable yet still hilarious, the supporting characters are all very interesting and then theres well... Claptrap.
The art style of this game is very nice making for some very beautiful areas, the use of colour is very good making for interesting beatiful areas to play in and explore, and well backtracking. Backtracking is the main problem in the game, you will find yourself going from one side of an area to the other as you go to a door, its stuck, travel across the area, to travel back to the door, then to go back to a teleporter then walk all the way to your quest giver to turn it in. This can get very annoying but you wont notice as you are just enjoying killing things on your way.
Each character is very lovable in their own way leading to some very fun quests from them. When you kill an enemy loot will just spew everywhere and you just want to check out what gun they dropped. The weapons in the game are randomally created leading to very intersting and great guns for your enjoyment.

This is (in my opinion) one of the greater games on Steam. For those who are looking for a TASTE of EVE here you go. This game is almost like a baby stepping stone into the EVE universe. While the game does have its flaws as I will state, I believe that this sandbox game has great potental. Now, I will say that I do not believe it is worth $40 just yet. The modding community has yet to take off and you can cheat the game by simply opening your save in Notepad++ and editing the data. Which I believe somewhat cuts the fun out of comparing achievements to other players globally. The missions of hunting the heros are somewhat wonky as well because it seems they jump systems if you watch the map. Just as well, there is a very large difficulty spike in the game that you must prepare for. As you reach a certain level your enemies gain vet rank and you probably have yet to make enough money to even afford a ship that can stand up to them. (Unless you did what I do and stole a ship from the pirates) Now for the positives. This game has BEAUTIFUL scenery. For an indie game, a lot of time was put into this game and its atmosphere. The story and voice acting are a bit stale, but the fact that they are there is awesome. And the story, while being a bit dry, actually does make some form of sense. So kudos! At the start of the game you may pick to be a captain, engineer or another class that excels in firing. You may hire mercenaries to board ships or even follow you in to battle which is what the captains perks stand for. The shooter class perks somwhat speaks for itself. But I played as an engineer as the perks seemed to outweigh the others. The story is the same regardless of your class, but each class has its own specialties with 4 main "moves" But those moves have 5 evolutions within each allowing you to alter them as you go to tailor your playstyle up to the max level of 80. There are a plethora of planets to explore as well as tons of ships to purchase and try out. All in all, if you enjoy sandbox style games and as well as enjoy the beauty of flight or space travel, I recommend this game. I also recommend trying it if your thinking about EVE online. This game is a MUCH simpler thing. But it has many of the same aspects as well as can help you decide if you would even enjoy the simple aspects of what EVE offers before you worry about the more complex matters.

Picked this up at EB for $28, and in all honesty, I got my moneys worth. Although short, with less than 20 missions in all, I found it quite good and enjoyable. The price steam has it is NOT worth it at all, try and find a physical copy or buy it on console or something, it's probably better to get it on that costwise.
Campaign Mode:
I never played BO1 properly, I played it at a friends house on his ps3, and my experience was very biased, as I had never played a CoD game before, they instructed me to die constantly, killing the experience for me. After playing through BO2's campaign, I have found one of my favourite single player experiences. I enjoyed the storyline, and the characters were great. The bonus(?) levels where you took control of multiple troops was one of my favourite experiences, as it reminded me of some of my favourite games. Like I said, the storyline is rather short, but it is very enjoyable.
Zombies Mode:
After playing Zombies for a bit, I found it quite enjoyable. I found myself playing the doom soundtrack in the background. Zombies mode is your run of the mill horde based zombie defence. Unlock new areas inside your map to make life easier or harder. Fun game mode, and in my opinion, its a good game to play when bored or depressed. It's a good time waster, and the slow moving zombies, tied in with the fact they explode when on fire, is quite funny.
And Finally, Multiplayer:
Multiplayer has to be one of the most fun online FPS experiences I've had since I first started CS:GO or TF2. I've had the same enjoyment that I've had whilst playing games like Doom 1. It started off a little slow and rocky, with everyone else having great weapons compared to my pleb tier weapons. After I hit level 4, I unlocked custom loadouts, letting me use my personal favourite weapon. The multiple game modes make for a fun experience. The only thing I would prefer is a better sever joining system, such as the ones in valve games. BO2's multiplayer server system is more of a wheel of fortune, roll and hope you get a full game.
All in all, Black Ops 2 is one of my favourite games to date, and it is definatley worth a buy if you get it on sale

Shallow gameplay, features that aren't implemented or badly and a general low quality feel to the game makes this no replacement for Freelancer or X. I don't know where to begin, so I'll just ejaculate my thoughts as they surface:
Ships, which range from sub-capitals (Gunships) to dreadnaughts, all feel like fighters. They've got turrets, but there's no feeling of "weight" behind it all. No tracking needed, stuff turns on a dime. Shield and armor feel useless. Fighters and bombers just "blip" into existence when you launch them. Worst of all is that you're made to believe this is a space game, yet there's no trace of inertia - shut off the engine and you come to a perfect stop. I'll admit that this is hardly the only game that's guilty of this faux pas, but it's extremely noticable in SG2. The main mode of travel, "power to engines", is slow and takes any feeling of fluidity out of playing.
Too many factions. All of them without any personality or motivations. Building up a reputation doesn't seem to do anything, and the game randomly turns them hostile or friendly towards the player during the storyline without any lasting damage or benefits. Devs, instead of having 36 factions (I'm not making this up), just have a couple of main players on the political stage and a few overt bad guys (Pirates + the Big Bad).
Quality of the game is lacking. Voice-acting is terrible, accompanied by large amounts of text between main missions. Do not play this game for the main campaign, for its storyline is the most blaise of generic sci-fi crap and daddy-issues (Which also assumes you have played the previous SG's campaign).
German and eastern European developers - stop using local "talent" as actors and writers. The accents are horrible ("Ze Germans are comingk!") and the amount of spelling errors and horrible construction of sentences in the written text makes me just wanna skip all the nonsense.
All of that, and it's not feature complete. There's this whole section of skills, perks and abilities (even a class) dedicated to fleet combat, but you're only ever in control of your own ship. You can hire mercenaries, but they require regular payment, you don't get a group of ships to command and control. Docking (or "anchoring" as its called in SG2) is non-existent, you just float up to a station and press a button. Not that stations are that necessary - they only feature to have a place to save the game, repair and rearm and buy crap.
tl;dr - vapid game devoid of any passion. Galaxy looks nice though!

This is my methadone to keep me going until Star Citizen is out.
TLDR: It's very relaxing and enjoyable to roam around popping pirate ships, and scooping up their loot while exploring each hex.
Theres some nice progression with levels earning you skills and perks to your character.  Meanwhile spend that ill gotten cash to upgrade ship systems, buy fancier guns, and stock up on consumables to give your ship an edge in a fight, or i suppose help miners in their tedious rock popping. Hire troops for the wetwork, bridge officers for passive bonuses, and later on mercenary captains to back you up in a fight. Remember, it's OK to leave them to die.  Ultimately earn enough (or take over!) that fancy new ship you've been eying. There are also purchasable licenses for financial perks like earning extra credits when killing certain factions or cheaper goods from a certain corporation, even passive credits per month so you can sit around and do squat and still earn money just like the one percenter you are.
Exploration stays enjoyable by providing several modes of travel.  Pay to use an established warp gate (there's a way to make a one time license purchase to make them free though), or risk some damage and redshirt lives by using wormholes.  There's also these odd green bands of gravitational anomolies than can pull you in and whip you across several sectors very quickly, and finally the convenience of a consumable that will jump you a limited distance but can go from anywhere to any place you've already explored (and have enough drives to reach). It's also financially useful as the more stations you find, the better options you'll have to buy low and sell high with a decent variety of trade goods, some of them illicit in certain regions.
I wish the different parts of space were more varied, but at least it's all uniformly pretty with nebulas, asteroid fields, ice asteroids, and clouds of floating junk (all mineable if you're into that sort of thing) to add some variety. There are scannable anomolies, though only a few types and they all just do some sort of passive thing to surrounding space like scramble sensors or block teleporters. Scanning them down will get rid of the field, and earn some xp and credits if its a mission, otherwise they are ignorable.  Some of the more unique stations are very beautiful, like the Spire, but most of the space stuff is pretty samey.
Combat is  pretty simplistic you can even (and its recommended) set your turrets to autofire and concentrate on turning your best shields towards the light show. I wish the different guns and damage types were a little more varied. Heavy weapons have limted ammo but help speed things up, and there are some other consumables that can be deployed to help increase offense or survivability.  Spice things up by locking your grappling array on a wounded ship and teleporting over boarding parties of expendable no name grunts who throw their lives away so you can get a big payday.  If you're lucky and manage to successfully take over a ship you get to loot it far more effectively that picking through its wreckage, then tow it to the nearest dock to either add to your stable or sell off. Remember to keep the redshirts stocked every time you come back to port. Out in the stars are a bunch of named elites with bounty's on their heads and suprisingly deadly offensive capabilities to test your mettle.
Currently theres no real story, and a very limited number of missions that just help earn credits while doing the things you're already doing, but the foundation that is there is solid and fun, and surprisingly well polished for an early access title.

When I first played this, my brother bought it, from a box, as the deckbuilding game. This you see however, is a virtual simulated version, of the EXACT same game!
If you don't have anyone to play against, and you love deckbuilding games, I suggest checking this out. It's got an interesting, unique twist, to the gameplay.
The entire GAME itself, is a tribute, to retro video games, due to it's sprite style. The difference? You PLAY the role of a boss-type enemy! You lure the "heroes" (adventurers) into your dungeon, try to set up rooms to lure them in, and if done right, you DEFEAT them! First one to defeat 10 adventurers, wins! But be warned; if an adventurer beats you 5 times, you're eliminated.
Don't be discouraged, now; this is a TRULY decent game! (In my opinion, anyway.) And please note on this; if you don't like deckbuilding games, or elimination based games, this is not the game for you. This is a great tabletop-to-PC card game.  Yes, this game is also a tabletop game.  I have the tabletop game and it's a great product.  Basically you play a dungeon boss, not a hero.  Your job is to lure heroes with treasure and build rooms in your dungeon to destroy those heroes.  If you succeed you gain a soul.  If the hero makes it through your dungeon you gain a wound.  Also you're competing with another dungeon boss.  Whoever has the most souls wins.  Because you're competing with another boss you can try to boost the heroes in you opponent's dungeon with spells to help them get through and cause your opponent to get a wound.  This game is turn-based so you get to set up your cards before any action happens.  Some of the card abilities can be used as the heroes are going through your dungeon.  This game isn't complicated.  It's easy to learn and the tutorial makes it easy to understand.

This is a prequel to the Arkham Series dating back to Year One of Batman. Generally, the developers of this game are not Rocksteady. Because of this, most Arkham fans pondered whether it is worth the money to preorder or not. Some, of course, don't have a brain to think and just preorder, crying with joy and bragging like brats. I bought the game after some videos and confirmations of its upcoming gameplay and dlcs. Season Pass is also bought too. This game has been worth the wait. Although, it reminds me of "The Dark Knight Rises" game app on the appstore.
The impact sounds are the same and the bridge are from The Dark Knight Rises.
The timeline in this game is a "younger" Bruce (Batman) who is more inexperienced than the one in Arkham City. This concludes that the Batman in Origins will be a bit slower in combat and has a brutal combat stance (due to his earlier age when he was more enraged at crime after his father and mother's death).
This game offers you a chance to play as deathstroke (If you preorder) and a chance to see Batman in his past.
Unfortunately, the game seems to have the same textures and buildings as Arkham City. On the bright side, they tweaked (from what I heard) over 300 things such as removing objects and replacing with snow and such to give a better "Year One" atmosphere.  Moreover, there are more thugs spawns everywhere and new types of enemies such as the "Martial Artists" whom can counter your attacks and strike back at you.
Personally, the game has its bugs and the developers have created a multiplayer mode which may inspire Rocksteady, who have hinted on another project which seems to be "bigger and better" as told by Kevin Conroy.
For anyone feeling the urge to brutally takedown thugs, beat combo scores, and the fluid combat system that Arkham City has excellently provided, play Arkham Origins.
This game may be game of the year but there is GTA V. Unfortunately, GTA V may not be GOTY, I assume, since it did not release on PC which is one of the most used possessions gamers have. Batman Arkham Origins have released games for Wii U, PC, Xbox 360, PS VITA, Nintendo DS, and PS3. Batman Arkham Origins: Blackgate is another game players should look at which has been released for PS VITA and Nintendo DS. There is also an app on the appstore for Batman Arkham Origins which has the same game mechanism and gameplay as the Batman Arkham City one (previous game app).
I have not reached the half of the game. All I can say is, there is significant amount of tasks to do and it clearly shows how much Batman needs to do AND done for Gotham City.
To the developers, congratulations on the game release. Of course, the bugs need to be fixed, but the amount of comments in the forums practically show that the game is incredible and "epic."
If you love the first game & Arkham City then you will love this one.

Overall this is a decent pool simulation, but I'm afraid that the same issues that apply to other pool and snooker simulators also applies here: the A.I doesn't simulate successful shots, but timed failures.
I'm at a stage in the game now where my opponents reliably get a break of three almost every time, and fail on the fourth shot.  So essentially three quality/flukey trick shots and a miss on a sitter.  I'm not sure why it is so difficult to program an A.I that simulates real players at different levels, though the best implementation of it I've seen is Virtual Snooker back in the DOS days.
There's also nobody online to play against, despite the game just coming off sale when you'd reckon most players are on it.  Perhaps a readout saying how many players are in the game interested in playing online would help rather than creating a room and nobody ever see it?
Remapping the "take a shot" button to a key doesn't work as the view moves in addition to the cue.  Using the mouse to take a shot seems too sensitive and you don't get the sense of pushing the cue that you do in Virtual Snooker.  Joypad seems to work better but moving your view around in a timed round is unworkable.
Overall I would recommend the game if on sale, but there are too many shortcomings to recommend it at full price.  Sorry developers.

This is the game I was hoping absolution would be. Large, open maps with a plethora of ways to complete ones objectives. A return to the old stealth system, rather than the weird situation in absolution where a disguise can often make it more difficult to infiltrate areas. The hint system can make it too easy but can simply be turned of thankfully, meaning you actually have to pay attention to your surroundings. Oh, and apparently 47 makes a pretty good model.

No number score because I have no set system for this stuff.

An entertaining, brain-teasing, pretty, well made game. I'm not too familiar with the classic Hitman titles, so I cannot compare. I only completed Absolution, and I find this one a better experience, it feels like a puzzle with multiple solutions, and it's fun to try them all. I think it works very well with the episodic release model, because it would leave a player with a single level until a new one is released. Willingly or not, he'll have time to learn the environment and try different approaches. In Absolution I personally was too focused on the story progression, and didn't care for the mechanics of the assasination - and when you rush through a level, you might miss a lot of fun. In this game it's quite different, it feels quite natural to replay the same mission multiple times; you memorise the events and characters, and see them from a different angle each time. Challenges stimulate you to try different approaches, but I wish some of them were not explained, leaving discovery of their meaning to the player (like hidden Steam achievements).
I do not experience any performance issues, I have GTX 960 and an old Phenom II x6 CPU, the game is locked in Low textures, but looks great and gives me an average of 40-50 fps in its benchmark. I switched to Exclusive Fullscreen mode for a smoother experience, and do not notice any lag or stuttering. No bugs either yet, touch wood. Online mode works fine for me, I don't see a problem in being connected while playing. Offline mode worked in beta, I expect it work here as well. So technically I have no complains.
But of course, as usual, most things related to Russia are wrong, sometimes so ridiculous - it's cute. I mean, people calling each other "comrade", privates telling a KGB general to shove off or saying "howdy" instead of saluting, Soviet vodka having a non-existent brand (and furthermore, a word that was invented about 10 years after), Soviet privates wearing sailors' vests... I think it was intended as a joke, really, it couldn't be so ridiculous on purpose. Or could it?..
Well, and if we're really nitpicking - I don't like the protagonist's voice much. The actor is somewhat straining to sound rough and tough, and it sounds cheap, more suited for a teenagers game like Borderlands or Bulletstorm. Agent 47 evidently has high intelligence, he acts with precision and focus - I'd expect him to speak in the same fashion. And his voice should be as unremarkable as his looks - to blend with any disguise. Good thing he doesn't speak much.
But all in all, I enjoy this game. I recommend it to anyone who likes stealth, puzzles and silenced pistols.

It's a sneaker-shooter, but it's better at the shooter aspect than the sneaker part:
Positives:
1) Shooter: Runs quickly,
2) Shooter: Shooting action is smooth, and headshots matter
3) Shooter: Has rewards for more thorough exploration (I found a hidden shotgun on the 2nd or 3rd level)
4) Sneaker: For sneaking, it... has vents.
Negatives:
1) Shooter: No health regens (or at least, not in the 1st few non-tutorial levels)
2) Sneaker: No shadows, so sneaking is line-of-sight - and the AI can detect you from two rooms away.
3) Sneaker: Even from two rooms away, the AI's "did I see that?" algorithm is just crazy fast.
So, if you're into shooters w/ some stealth, go for it.
If you're into pure stealth, look somewhere else.
I'm much more into sneaking than shooting, so I've gotta give it a downvote, but YMMV.

Originally a 5 chapter browser game available on newgrounds, now made its way on steam in a standalone version with some extra features.
Out of all the ‘retro’ styled games that try to mimic the feel of previous eras in gaming this title is one of the few successful games to actually pull it off, from the graphics, to the music and the simplicity on it’s gameplay, it’s well executed all around but doesn’t pretend to be anything beyond a top down shooter.
It takes some ideas from old Sci-Fi stereotypes and it’s amusing on its execution. Vaporizing weapons, Russians on Venus, Ninjas, a protagonist rockin’ a hair style, you name it. It provides some good chuckles and the game doesn’t take itself seriously, is all for fun and the game is a good time, albeit a bit repetitive after a while.
It offers a good challenge, especially on the Hard Mode which is available for this version of the game after beating it for the first time, the difficulty can be a bit frustrating, especially on the latter levels on Hard Mode, but the game has a checkpoint system and infinite life’s,  so it doesn’t become infuriating.
It’s not a long game, and I managed to get all achievements in less than 5 hours, but the price tag is fair for what it offers, I think the creator deserves some credit, and if you’re unsure about it, you can try the original browser version of the game (Which goes under the same name) and make your opinion out of it, that’s how I made my choice to purchase it and I don’t regret it.

Take Assassin's Creed, Shadow of Mordor, and The Batman Arkham Games' style of open-world exploration and thingamabob collection and inject it into the Legend of Mad max Rockatansky. You're not an elite assassin, supernaturally powered dead man, nor a playboy millionaire with loads of gadgets: you play as a brawler that likes fast cars and little else. The mechanics reflect this and perhaps out of all the Ubisoft-styled brand of world exploration, it makes the most sense (or has been the most sensibly implemented) in this game. This game is pretty much what you see is what you get. It will break no boundaries but it does not need to. It offers you fast cars, awesome landscapes, and the booming sounds of revving engines and discharging firearms.
Mark, it is not a tie-in to Fury Road. Go in expecting it to be what it is: yet another story of the legend of Mad Max. This game, for me, is a joy to play and I cannot ask more of it

The story of Spec Ops: The Line is somewhat different from your average shooter game. While you get to kill everyone you see, you don't get to be a hero for it. At times though, it feels a bit artificial and i could not quite immerse in the story. This maybe because it is sometimes quite brutal in showing the consequences of... well, killing everyone. I really enjoyed the imagery used in the game and the composition of colors. It was just nice to look at (at least while it didn't show you burned corpses and the like). The level design itself was rather linear though. The music is really awesome and reminded me instantly of the game's inspiration, Apocalypse Now.
What i really didn't like about the game were it's technical shortcomings (which mostly deduce from it being released on console aswell). The thing that annoyed me the most were the controls. I don't know how many times i was killed because the same button is used for cover and sprint. Actually even console controllers should have enough buttons, so why not just use different buttons ffs? Anti-aliasing would have been nice, but apparently consoles don't have it, so neither has the pc version. Last but not least, while the main character was high detail, everything else wasn't. The textures used on the environment were rather muddy, even for a 2012 title.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.
