That's what it's all about here, not the background-story, not the simplistic graphics, not the nice music. You're in some espionage situation and have to get deeper into the building, level by level. For this, reach the exit-elevator that is clearly identified by an ambient sound with a conveniently big radius. On the first floors, this is only a matter of getting there despite the guards, but later you need to find one or more generic credentials objects that allow you to proceed.
You can play the game stealthily or can go all out, but the latter is not recommended against guards since their bullets travel instantly. Bots, however, have slower shots, so you can make use of the evade-feature which causes an agile side-step, very useful. A shootout with guards is feasible, too, if you make use of cover and are lucky enough not to attract too many at once ...
If you die, you start over at the elevator. Since some levels are longer, this is a source of frustration, so one or two autosave-spots would have been nice.
The gameplay is minimalistic but somewhat fun and is carried by the wish to get deeper into the building, which I believe might lower the replay-value.
The levels are full of decorative objects, but they are all dead, there's no interaction. You can pick them up and throw them, and there's appropriate physics, but the lack of interactivity and everything in the same color makes it feel a bit "empty".
Fire extinguishers are red! But do they behave differently? Nope. They are just tossables, like everything else. No matter how many bullets you fire at them, they won't explode.
There are decorative vending machines that even spawn tossable cans, but the cans could as well be rocks. Toilets can be flushed. Wash basins can be "used". Paper towel dispensers also show some interaction. You can pick out toilet paper rolls from the stalls, which turns them into physical objects (e.g. you can shoot at them, making them fly around).
You can find radios from time to time (whose sound attenuation is ridiculously extreme). I was holding a radio when entering the lift to the next level, but when the loading was complete, my hands were empty. But you keep your weapons / ammo, same when you die.
And OMG there are some traps in the levels ... xD You'll know.
You can walk and run, which is a toggle or only temporary, this can be defined in the options. Same for crouching. Running isn't really fast, it's relaxed jogging. Sadly, there's no sprint feature, so while traversing longer stretches, I felt a bit imprisoned.
Walking diagonally makes you faster, which is a typical beginner mistake. Then again, Eidos Montreal made it, too, in Deus Ex: Mankind Divided.
You can also jump and crouch. I wish there was also mantling, because there are a few situation where, if you had proper arms :P, you should be able to get to that place (e.g. in the vents).
You can peek to the left and right. This seems to be unconditionally safe.
You can't holster your weapon, not that it really matters.
Your current weapon sways when you walk/run, but there's no option to make the camera sway. I miss that nowadays, seems to be a trend not to include it, probably because people are too inept to tune their setups optimally ("Waaah, I couldn't play this game, it made me dizzy!"), e.g. FOV still seems to be a book with seven seals even though it's all quite
really. Always with the lowest common denominator. :( Can a guy be accused of becoming somewhat elitist under these circumstances?
You start with 100 health, which decreases as you are attacked, and you die when it reaches 0. No health recharge, and no pickups that heal you. - Score one for realism.
The use-key picks up objects, and then you can throw them (Left mouse button.) or drop them again (Right mouse button.), and it's really annoying that you can't use the use-key, too, to drop them.
The input keys can be changed (and by now, indeed the right shift key can be assigned, too, so I changed from a WASD-centric config to arrow keys; the keypad enter does not seem to be different from the main enter, but that's not fatal), but texts on screen are hard-coded, they do not reflect the current key configuration.
When assigning the left mouse button (which you probably don't want to, because it's fine as the fire control), upon release of the button, the assign function will be called again immediately, so you have to move the mouse to the side of the controls before releasing the button.
The volume sliders are of course broken like in 99% of all other games. They'd need to raise the slider's value (assuming it's a float from 0 to 1) to the power of Euler's number (~2.7) before applying it to the sound, or the "infinite" power of zero will make it like it currently is, namely that the top 30% of the sliders do almost nothing, and the closer to 0 you get, the more powerful the sliders' effect. (The non-linearity of human hearing that people keep bringing up here is not relevant. That's people for ya. They don't know what they're talking about and feel free to repeat what they heard somewhere.)
The sound fx are functional and slightly avant-garde styled (e.g. the jump sound with its fast echo). Sadly, tossed objects don't make any impact sound. That would even feel wrong if tossing an object would
lure guards to the point of impact.
The music is quite good really, albeit its style might be a wee bit too foreground-ish, but it's within limits. I think there are several music tracks, but they only play rarely. There's no "They're on to you!" music like in many other games, and I wouldn't call that a mistake. I wish those other games had an option to turn off this context-sensitivitiy, because it gives away information you otherwise wouldn't have. Hey, I recommend that when you re-play your favorite games, turn off their music for once and listen to something else, e.g.
, which kinda goes with everything.
Well, you're in a virtual world, so the bland schematics-like graphics make sense (but not the objects :P). Ultimately, it's about gameplay, so while the graphics are a bit
abstract to me, they don't really stand in the way of the game being enjoyable.
Except the vents are extremely same-y, it all looks the same, the only orientation help are the paths they take, the occasional (rare) fan, and some environmental sounds (e.g. vicinity of exit-elevator). I hope they spice those up slightly later on.
The graphics options do what they should, e.g. the antialiasing works just as expected. Sadly, the bloom option is too strong, I hope they add some kind of slider or at least a weaker version. I ended up playing without it.
The FOV slider is THE FINGER (You know, the middle one.) to the whole industry! Know why? Because it goes straight up from 1° to 179°! Yes, you heard that right. Plus it seems to be vertical FOV, in which case a wider screen would automatically give you a wider view, not that it would be important with this mother of all FOV sliders.
The engine or the maps could be optimized a bit better: It's all smooth most of the time, but I did notice some lower FPS dips sometimes. It's not my PC: DX:MD all ultra in FullHD minus MSAA and VolLight @60FPS. So a game with spartan graphics like this one should be all smooth all the time. (I had all graphics settings to the max, except bloom off.)

ETS2 is the top notch of most driving simulators, with amazing graphics and gorgeous scenary.
The map is a downscaled representation of Europe and covers (fully or partially) most of the countries.
The base game has: Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Poland, Slovakia, Switzerland and United Kingdom.
DLC has added more towns to the: Czech Republic, Poland and Slovakia.
And it also added Hungary.
DLC added: Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
In the game you have the ability to drive the most popular trucks in Europe: Scania, Volvo, Mercedes Benz, MAN, DAF, Renault, IVECO.
Beside the great base models, the modding community has brought hundreds of great mods that you can download and use in your game, from maps to accesories and trucks.
With the ETS2MP (Euro Truck Simulator 2 Multiplayer) mod, you have the ability to play along hundreds of other players.
Since the release of the game SCS Software has countinously updated and improved the game, even after the release of American Truck Simulator ETS will surely keep be updated for the next year or 2.

Rust is honestly one of the best survival games out - and much like other survival games out there it takes time to understand the basics of resource griding and crafting. Rust in my honest opinion is best played with a group of people, if you're going solo try pick a smaller pop server until you get some experience.
The basis of rust is -
1. Resource Grind
2. Crafting your base
3. Survival
4. PVP / Raiding other bases
You're going to find out very quickly that in most servers shoot on sight is going to be standard, don't expect to go into a server and expect your first encounter is going to be friendly, it most likely won't be. People want your resources, especially in the early grind.
Servers will reset depending on the admin, allowing everyone to restart new. This can vary between a week or a month.
The game from my short time of play-time has shown me the dev's are continiously developing the game which is good, a few veteran's of rust have said over the last few months alot of updates have been happening and the player count is impressive.
Beware though, as like every other survival game out there - hackers can be a problem.
Also servers sometimes have a tendency to have memory leaks which can cause mass lag - but other then that it runs well for the most of the time. Also regarding servers, check when the restart of a server will happen, there is nothing quite like spending a whole day upgrading a base and then finding out the server resets the next day.
With a GTX 1080 I can have this game with most of the high settings although crop in can be a pain at times with my FPS dropping from 100 to 10 in a matter of seconds regarding loading.
In anycase, a sold game and worth the asking price. Hopefully the game will continue to develop and expand whilst fixing the issues.

On the plus side, I have the card-based version of Boss Monster, and the PC version seems like a fun adaptation, maintaining and even amplifying the sense of humor displayed by the card version. The graphics are adequate (it's based on a card game which is in turn inspired by old-school video games), the sound effects are nothing special but they add a little more spice to the experience, and it's generally an enjoyable game.
However, this game definitely needs some more work. Most damaging is the fact that at least on my computer, the point-and-click interface does NOT match up with where you actually see most of the buttons on the screen; it defaulted to full-screen view and made the critical error of assuming I had a widescreen display (which I don't), and the misalignment between "pointing" and "clicking" meant that it took some trial and error to get to the options menu. Switching to windowed mode DID lessen the issue, but there are still a few places where the spot you need to click doesn't actually correlate with the item you're trying to click on.
Overall, I have to say that Boss Monster is enjoyable if you're willing to forgive its flaws - and honestly, for a five-dollar game, some forgiveness is PROBABLY in order. However, I'd be much happier (and much more likely to play more of it, not to mention buying DLC) if the developers would actually pop the hatch and try to improve on what they've got here. It still needs some work, budget game or not.

This game is a gem, because not only that it is based on the Star Wars universe, but it has the best and most rewarding light saber combat system from all the SW games. It is a story driven action game in which you get to be a Jedi apprentice at Luke Skywalker's Academy.
You can customize your Jedi hero by choosing the gender, race, clothing, and then choose your light saber (hilt and color). Only the Jedi colors (no red) are available in single player, including Mace Windu's purple. The saber can be upgraded later on to staff or dual sabers, which is awesome.
By doing missions, you get to choose between light and dark force powers, like heal, mind trick, force lightning. These can be upgraded with time, while the "core" powers (jump, push, pull, etc), upgrade automatically with your in game progression.
After several missions you become a jedi knight and you can upgrade your sword to Darth Maul's staff, or dual wielding light sabers. Again you get to pick the colors, you can have a blue and green sword if you like. Each saber style has it's own combo moves, the jedi can do lots of acrobatics with the saber which need some time to get used with, but after some practice they add a lot to the combat system.
The missions are varied, you even get to ride creatures or vehicles. Some missions are quite long and you get to kill lots of imperial troops. However they aren't boring because with time you get to fight more and more sith. The light saber duels are the best part of this game. Sometimes these fights can be quite unpredictable, you can die quite fast or waste two sith warriors at once in a spectacular combo in Matrix style slow motion. You also get to meet several key figures from the Star Wars universe, like Luke, Chewbacca, Kyle Katarn (from previous SW games), and Boba Fet. In the last missions the sith you will meet can be quite challenging, but this only makes the game more interesting. The music is of course the music from Star Wars, it is epic..

What a great Star Wars adventure! I originally got this game way back in 2011 but never bothered to finish it due to some silly mission I was stuck in - I'm glad that Steam saved my game files so I could finally get back around to it. And oh man, what have I been missing - this game is just amazingly fun.
On your travels as jedi academy student Jaden Korr you'll be under the tutelage of Kyle Katarn (the protagonist of the Jedi Knight series) and Luke Skywalker himself facing enemies such as the Imperial Remnants and the Disciples of Ragnos (evil Jedi with force powers). The storyline is pretty simplistic, but it has its moments including fighting a top a moving tram and escaping from a mutated Rancor while it breaks the entire level apart.
The game has a system where you can play the levels in any order which really helps with the pacing - apart from the few ridiculous "the ground is lava" and "defuse all the bombs hidden in the level" missions, they're all very enjoyable and have great level design. The villain is pretty generic and dull, but since the nature of the game is varied missions directed from the Jedi Academy it doesn't really need a strong plotline with interesting characters. Only little complaint was that the later levels have a lot of annoying Force Jump puzzles (even a conveyor platforming puzzle level, come on now).
The lightsaber combat makes the game - the actual first person shooter mechanics are okay at best, but the sheer fun factor of the game comes from slicing and dicing your enemies with your lightsaber, flipping around the map with awesome Force powers. You can force choke, shoot lightning out of your hands and flip across walls. You can customize your character and even change the color of your lightsabers. Around the halfway point of the game (as you ascend to the position of a Jedi Knight) you can choose a single lightsaber, dual lightsabers or a double lightsaber. I played through the game with dual lightsabers and it was really fantastic how each of the lightsaber styles have their own movesets and mechanics to use.
The multiplayer of the original is long dead but the modding community still has a few servers up - I recommend the "Movie Battles 2" mod for a great Star Wars experience that showcases the battles of the universe, and for people that like the original trilogy, you can duel Luke Skywalker vs Darth Vader in the "Movie Duels 2" mod.
The game hasn't aged as much as I thought it had. There's a little labyrinthe level design in the missions, but otherwise it's a quality Star Wars adventure that won't leave you cold - interesting combat, timeless setting and just plain fun gameplay. Go get it!

Combat is somewhat confusing at first but the games excellent tutorial guide and fully customizable control menu is very helpful.
Pros:
-Good graphics.
-Intense space combat.
-Can easily change viewing settings - Rudder control"bridge" view, Rudder control third person view, and turret third person view.
-Ability to purchase and upgrade several starships.
-Can hire mercs and form a fleet.
-Large open world to explore.
-Many unique ways to "jump"around the map e.g. rifts and wormholes.
-Story is ok.
-Background music is pretty good and varied.
Cons:
-No NPCs to interact with at space stations.
-No first person perspective.
-No ship interior perspective.
Mixed:
-Fairly steep learning curve to become proficient with all of the games functions.
Overall a great indie title!  Give your self lots of time to play this game...it is hard to quit this game for the night!

My original (thumbs down) review was:
"If I ever had any love for this game, it was killed with the last boss fight."
And somehow I still stand by this. If you don't think boss fights are fun (like me), you don't want to play the ending of this game. But there are many aspects in the game I like - for example, it's up to you how you tackle the levels: you can be sneaky, but you can also go on a rampage. A combination is wise, too. Each level is short enough to let you actually enjoy the lack of save/load - it gets intense this way, and challenging. ROOT focuses on this experience, and that's what makes it mostly cool experience.
But there are also many things I'd like to see changed - the boss fights are the best example. But also the fact that the levels all look quite the same. You can change the wall colors, which is a nice touch, but I wonder why the developers didn't adjust the colors for each level, to make them more distinct. (I also wonder about their choice of standard color. It's a bit ugly.) The controls felt awkward, at least at the beginning, and some keys seem to be superfluous. Enemies see you miles away, which makes sense, because you can shoot them at once, but especially with the small spiders it's awful to shoot them while they're only a pixel high.
I'm also quite sad that there is a lot of wasted potential; ROOT has a lot of objects in the levels, but interaction with them is either meaningless "flush the toilet" or "take and throw it". There could have been more, like traps and bridges, etc. And then there are some scripted events, e.g. a creature climbs up a wall and escapes, and later is never mentioned again. (Or I missed something?)

ROOT is a fun and (very) challenging FPS unlike any you've ever played. The biggest thing to remember is that ROOT is neither run 'n gun, or stealth. Rather it is a mixture of both, and you cannot succeed by doing just one or the other. The key in ROOT is to strategize your moves. Think, then act. Don't act, then think. That, and commit to your actions. If you make the choice to enter and clear a room, commit to that choice and don't half♥♥♥♥♥it. Those are my tips for you.
ROOT is definitely a unique game. For one thing, the game takes place inside of a computer system as you, "Edward Summerton" (creative name, developers), attempt to hack your way in. Data and security software is manifested as objects and enemies.
There are three weapons in ROOT. A nightstick, which can be used to silently subdue enemies from behind. A pistol, which is accurate at all ranges but does low damage. And a shotgun, which is (obviously) best at close range but does high damage. Weapon handling is different from most shooters in that there is no recoil, reticle spread, or ironsights, and your shots are placed exactly where you put the cursor. This makes your ability to aim of absolute importance, as you can't simply panic-fire and count on spread to make some of your shots  hit the target.
This is a game that forces the player to tread softly if they want to survive. Nearly all of the enemies you will face are stronger than you and you must be on the alert, constantly scanning for threats. It is, however, not difficult to hide from these enemies if you memorize their patterns and know what to do. Most of the AIs are exceedingly stupid, and can be thwarted so long as you remain calm and take things slow.
Overall, ROOT is a very fun game that I reccomend to anyone looking for a change of pace in an FPS game. Although bare in mind that it is a frustrating game; you will likely die... a lot. The end boss is especially difficult, but he can be beaten if you persevere. I definitely encourage you to give this one a try, especially if you are bored with the run-of-the-mill shooters, and want something different.

Starpoint Gemini 2 is a game that I really want to like. The combat is fun, the graphics are good, and the open world is pretty...err... pretty, even though it is incredibly static with things like planetary rotation and many animations left completely out.
Despite my attempts to like the game, there was one thing that haunted me as I played this game. I could not stop asking myself "why?"
Why did I want to tumble through space doing bounties and moving cargo? The story is flat out bland and totally uninteresting, with a typical "avenge my father who the baddies killed" revenge plot (and one of the most rigid and uninspiring protagonists I have ever seen in any game, and the supporting characters are worse by several great orders of magnitude), and the lack of true player enterprise in the sandbox give you no reason to want to progress in this game. Sure, you buy bigger ships and do bigger missions, but what then? Can I take political control of systems and build my own faction? No. Can I buy property and create a business empire and compete with other traders or corporations? No. All the player can really do is just fly missions and shoot stuff, and then get bigger ships to fly bigger missions and shoot bigger stuff.
The developers are great, and really work hard (and continue to do so), and I really wish I could give this a positive review, but the fact of the matter is the game is just "meh" on most accounts. Without anything to really motivate me all I could do was let my mind drift to the impression that I was just in a giant empty MMO were I had to play by the AI factions' rules. But I saw no good reason for it to be that way with no player interaction of any sort.
So I don't think its an entirely bad game, but as I have no desire to go play it anymore until there is something to motivate me to progress in the game, I don't feel I would be totally honest in recommending it.

I didn't play the board game, but so far I really enjoy the video game version. To be honest, it is easier for me to find friends with whom I can have a video gaming night than a board gaming night, especially when the game can be played online. I payed the game less than 2$ a few nights ago and already played much more than I would have in a year with a board game, and it's only the beginning!
This game is all about managing your cards well, and you will rarely find yourself in a situation in which you can do nothing. There's always a way to catch up other players.
There are a two majors flaws:
-The tutorial is incomplete and you will learn a lot of rule on the spot, but that's ok. In a video game, I expect to learn a bit of the game every time I play it; in a board game, this would be frustrating, and I would blame the owner of the game for not explaining the rules clearly.
-There's a timer for every action. It's there to make sure every players had the time to read the card (be it a spell or a room ability) so they can themselves play a card to counter it. It's annoying, because some periods are way too short (for example, when you have to choose what five out of seven cards you will keep at the beginning of a match) but some others last too long and can't be skipped. For example, when a hero advances in a dungeon, it waits a few seconds in every room. If no other player has a (useful) spell to play, there's no point in seeing this. If this could be skipped, especially in single-player mode, it would be wonderful.
The first problem gets better as you play more and learn more about the game. The second problem is pretty annoying, but the issue with "too short" phases probably will diminish as I know the cards more, and the issue with the "too long" phases will probably remain an issue, but eh, in the end, it still goes faster than in real life, without all the computation and shuffling to do.
Also, the developers listen to the players and make improvements on the game based on their feedback, so there's hope that it will change.
So far, every matches I had was interesting, and it was all close victories (unlike a certain Munchkin...).

Short review:
Card game where you entice adventurers into your dungeon to kill them. While the game mechanics seem fun, I strongly do not recommend this game because the game UI is so horribly buggy and slow it's completely unfun to play.  Even if you got this game for free, I would recommend you spend your time elsewhere.
Long review:
It's a competitive card game where you draw cards representing rooms and spells, trying to entice adventurers into your dungeon so you can kill them, and trying to help adventurers survive / not enter your opponents' dungeons.
You get 5 slots on the board to build rooms in, you can stack rooms on top of eachother. Rooms have items associated with them, and adventurers pick the dungeon with the most of their desired item to enter.
You draw one room per turn, and you get to play one room per turn. Some rooms have special abilities, and you can get spell cards that do special stuff too.
I really loved the concept of this game, and mechanically it seemed like something that would be fun and interesting to play. Unfortunately the UI design absolutely killed any hope I had of enjoying the game.
Each time an adventurer enters a dungeon, it has to step through each of the player's rooms (up to 5). But in each room the game provides a few seconds for players to decide if they want to play a spell or activate a room ability. Which doesn't sound that bad - except an average game has 15-30 adventurers, and 90% of the time you don't have anything you want to do during the wait period. These few seconds per step add up to a ton of time sitting there thinking "hurry up, come on already" - extremely aggrivating.
You interact with the game by dragging cards around. You drag your rooms onto the board slots for them, you drag your spells onto the center to cast them, etc. Except the UI constantly screwed up what card I was trying to pick. I'd click and drag on a card, and constantly end up with the wrong card landing. Sure it's easy to undo that positioning, but at the same time it's annoying - especially when it felt like it was happening about 1/3 of the time.
It really is too bad the game is so hard to interact with. The card game behind it all seems quite fun. As I mentioned in my short review, I strongly do not recommend this game, even if you get it free your time is better spent elsewehre.

I'm not seeing one single review about the game itself, so let's fix this. Don't listen to them, this game does not deserve to be marked as "mixed", it's really awesome. As a Hitman fan, this is the game I was waiting for after the Absolution letdown. Yes, there is only one map at the moment, but GOD ! It's so huge, so full of possibilities. As someone who has played and enjoyed blood money multiple times, I can confidently say that this game is worthy of the hitman title so far - if one ignores performance issues
Enviroments are rich with fire alarms to pull, chandeliers to drop, drinks to poison (even non-targets as well) etc etc. The Paris map is of a good size, its not "massive" but it would be a larger than average level compared to previous games. (And after several run throughs myself and with friends, I am still discovering new things)
The guard ai is fun as well- they will react differently based on situation. If you walk into a trespass zone from a safe zone, they might simply escort you out of the area. If you are in a higher security zone, they will attempt to arrest you. If there is an alert going, they will simply kill you. You can trick them with coins or dropping items, allowing fun ai breaking strategies.
Combat and Movement- Combat retains the easy to use controls of Absolution. Lets face it, earlier hitmans were overall rather clunky. This game is not. 47 moves and acts very fluidly, minimizing frustrating mistakes.
Combat itself is a cross between Blood Money and Absolution. In the right spot, you can drop them one after another fairly easily, like in BM, but they will still spread out and try to pin and flank you, like in Asolution. Unlike both games, you can only take a couple of bullets before death.
TL:DR
Peformance is an issue, gameplay is not
-Detailed and rich level design with numerous approaches and gameplay styles supported
-Blood Money gameplay w/Absolution controls
-Solid and scaled guard ai (will react differently based of off situation)
-Arguably best control in series (47 reacts fluidly and controls are not at all clunkly imo)
-Best combat in series (Enemies pin and flank, 47 is just as vulnerable to gunfire as enemies)

What else can I really say....it's another call of duty game.
Story
------
The story is rather interesting connecting some of the story to black ops, however there are some parts that leave you with questions or why things are playing out the way there are. Either way there is a bit more developed story compared to previous Call of duty games, there is also side operations and the ability to change the outcome of your story leading to multiple endings let them be good or bad which is a nice touch to add for a series aiming towards consequences.
Gameplay
----------
Like any other Call of duty game, there isn't much change to the gameplay that I have noticed, there is of course new guns, abilities but it still leaves that feeling that nothing was really added when it comes down to combat. For the way missions are played out however is really nicely done having the option before the mission to switch out your loadout to grab weapons you prefer as well as encourage you to keep playing to unlock certain weapons. The side operations allow you to go in with a team of soldiers to take out a target but remember you have limited lives and time so move fast and fight hard.
The feeling of choice has truly been added to call of duty but the question is how long will it last, the newest call of duty goes back to the follow the trail.
Conclusion
=========
I could go on and on but come on....it's a call of duty game what else can you really add to series that keeps moving the story but combat and certain game mechanics continue to stay the same...of course the golden rule "if ain't broken why fix it" but still more risk needs to be added like throwing your gun at your enemy to knock them down just to run up to them and shove your size 12 boot in his face or hack their helmet to find enemy locations for a few minutes or secs. There is a lot that can be added but risk has to be taken.
If you like Call of duty series = Buy it
If you like the online aspect = Buy it the story will give you a few minutes or hours of fun.
If your not a big fan of call of duty = Save your money until a sale
If your poor = Save your money
If you have no clue what to buy and just looking at reviews to make a decision for you = Get a relationship or married it will help make those decisions for you :).

This game takes on both the FPS genre and RPG and mashes the two together to create something great.
You explore the giant world of Pandora, killing most things in your way. The game is whacky and completely nuts, you will open LOTS and LOTS of containers and everytime you walk up to one, even small ones you will be excited for what is inside it - even though it is probably just some ammo. Even though the game is nuts the charactars themselves are great, along with the plot. You will find yourself laughing at the stupidity of the game one moment then being drawn into the plot the next. Handsome Jack, the villian of the story is a great villian, he is crazy and hateable yet still hilarious, the supporting characters are all very interesting and then theres well... Claptrap.
The art style of this game is very nice making for some very beautiful areas, the use of colour is very good making for interesting beatiful areas to play in and explore, and well backtracking. Backtracking is the main problem in the game, you will find yourself going from one side of an area to the other as you go to a door, its stuck, travel across the area, to travel back to the door, then to go back to a teleporter then walk all the way to your quest giver to turn it in. This can get very annoying but you wont notice as you are just enjoying killing things on your way.
Each character is very lovable in their own way leading to some very fun quests from them. When you kill an enemy loot will just spew everywhere and you just want to check out what gun they dropped. The weapons in the game are randomally created leading to very intersting and great guns for your enjoyment.

All in all CS:GO is a good FPS for many reasons. Offering multiple different maps and game modes, it is also a great baseline game to practice your FPS skills, from gamesense and decision making all the way to aiming mechanics and proper peeks. I've used community workshop maps in this game to improve my skill in other games as well. However, CS:GO competitive mode is not for every one. If that is the main reason you are thinking about buying this game please take these factors to note.
1.) The game is dying competiviely at lower ranks. Throwers, leavers and hackers are becoming even more apparent especially if you don't have prime matchmaking, which requires you to have a certain amount of time played, as well as an activated phone that can recieve sms messages. Without prime, your match experiences are going to be FAR more negative than they otherwise would be.
2.)Smurfing is a HUGE problem in this game. If your goal is to get better at FPS's I would highly recommend that you not do it in a competive scene, but rather set the bots to hard, or download a workshop map specifically designed for what skills you need to work on.
Here is my Pro Con list for the game overall.
Pros:
1.)Weapon Skins out the booty
2.)GREAT for improving overall FPS skills
3.)Immersive competitive feel
4)Hit Detection and Bullet Reg. is great
5.)Good time killer and troll outlet
Cons:
1.)Competitive is a negative experience if you are easily offended by other peoples ideas or thoughts. Half of the matches you join, you will be surrounded by arguing teammates due to this reason. This leads to a decline of team morale, which people ALWAYS seem to forget can turn a game 180 degrees. It is difficult to play inteligently or do anything reasonably for that matter while blinded by emotion. If you are an emotionally driven person, COMP IS NOT FOR YOU.
2.)dem knives are cute AND expensive bb
3.)Grindy learning curve, especially if you are brand new to PC gaming
4.)It's impossible to roll gloves in a case (not really im just mad i haven't yet)
Overall, CS:GO is a relatively expensive, but very well put together FPS. If you are into FPS games you should enjoy this game, and I would highly recommend it.

I am pleasantly surprised by this game.  Normally I eschew console games as they tend to have a very different design culture from PC-centric games (IOW, they suck) but this one is pretty decent.  Yeah the combat is repeatative but its not boring me - I think mainly because the game doesn't actually force you to fight every 30 seconds.
It works decently with a M/KB - even the vehicles.  'Fishing for men' is freaking hilarious.  Though if there's a negative in the gameplay itself its the modern thing of putting in a game mechanic but not having the balls to make it matter - you need fuel for the car, you'll never be short of it though so there's no point in a fuel meter.  You use water to heal - but you're never short of it.  Even ammo is easy to get after few hours.
It ain't all good though.  Those unskippable splash screens leading to a 'press any key to continue'♥♥♥♥♥♥  The restricted FOV.  HOLDING A KEY DOWN TO COMPLETE A GENERIC ACTION???!!!  WTF did that start being a thing?  Weird decision to change which key does a context sensitive function - 'E' to 'use' most things but 'R' to enter or exit a vehicle?  Its a console game, through and through.
And the loading times are insane on SSD along with no 'save anywhere'.
How can peasants tolerate that sort of crap?
Overall though - if its on sale its a solid buy,

I think it has something to do with the developers being active on the forums, big-upping anyone that says anything positive. Will update this review if my opinion changes, but I have a pretty good picture of the core dynamics: capture till you get a bigger ship, capture till you get a bigger ship until you get the biggest ship. Do really boring missions until you get your rank up. Otherwise you might do the really boring version of trading or mining (compared to other games).
Overall I think a game like Starsector has far more RPG depth.

Loved this game. Felt like Privateer 2 without the cutscenes and sadly missing Clive Owen with Christopher Walkins :-( Freelancer should've been more like this. SG2 is a lot more open world than Freelancer which has its advantages and disadvantages. Personally, I found it purely an advantage. Unlike Privateer 2 and Freelancer you can truly just be a merchant if you want and switch effortlessly to being a badass kill everything murder ship at any space station/planet. Sometimes it's just the little things that make you happy... The graphics are great, the music not annoying, the abundance/ease of quickly accepting missions is a serious plus, and most importantly the flexibility of the game to allow someone the ability to play  the game how they want w/out the need of trainers, cheat codes, or cheat engine.
Just like in the real world there are easy ways to make a quick buck with minimal returns or riskier methods that garnish heavy monetary rewards. I love that this game isn't afraid to make the playing field drastically uneven when it comes to rewards. Harder, almost always (there are times you get lucky/learn to exploit advantageous situations), means greater rewards! Learning the in game market is very beneficial. But it gets better, should you disagree w/me all you have to do is download any of the many mods and change how the game mechanics work. This game is a literal win-win. Small minor bonus pluses that I think are worth mentioning are; 1.) Achievements actually give you in game bonuses 2.) Blueprints that give better stuff that can't be bought 3.) Bounty hunting ( this is a mixed bag. this system could better implemented but I'll be damned if i didn't end up hunting everyone down!) 4.) Buying of certificates/licenses (w/game money and not real money) that give-in game bonuses for no other reason but to make the game fun (personally, I think it could have been better implemented but I sure as♥♥♥♥♥♥was excited to find a new one!). 5.) A good array of ships to pick from (potentially unlimited if you count mods... Just saying...) 6.) Personally, I found the system upgrade gimmick confusing at 1st but once understood, it opens the door to a lot of options that becomes unlimited if you include modding (just saying...).
No game is perfect and this one isn't either. This is the disadvantage section of SG2. SG2 has some pretty poor optimization problems. 4-5 years ago my PC was a champ so it's aged a bit meow. Still, w/the level of graphics/visuals/objects it should run better. Especially since the video/graphics adjustment is bugged/non-functional. It's only a moderate complaint because the game allows mods and several are designed to reduce the toll taken on your PC. The rest of the comaplaints are mild at best because all are easily adjusted w/mods or are drastically overshadowed by the game's massive, bulging, make you scream in your pillow as you take it awesomeness so here goes- 1.) The voicovers are almost all a joke. They're done w/the stalest emotion possible. 2.) The story is kinda flat. Open ended games are prone to this a lot so it obviousley shouldn't be a huge unseen problem here. The game brings up interesting things here and there so kudos for the Devs for trying but it is still kinda... ummm... blah most of the time (kudos for the DEVs for doing such a good job to make the game so fun I really didn't care!)
In short, my complaints are minimal at best and I had countless hours of fun playing it. I found it quick and easy to learn and SG2 left a lot of options for me to explore for future play throughs. I can't ask a game to do more than that but w/mods this game could be literally different everytime I played. I got it on sale and felt like I stole something. I would have happily paid full price and been more than content. This game is awesome, WOOF!

Spec Ops: The Line is a decent game, but that is about it.
It has an untypical storyline compared to most other military shooters out there, which makes it stand out from the crowd.
However, gameplay-wise it is just your average cover-based modern military TPS.
Dash to cover, shoot some enemies, change cover, rinse and repeat throughout the whole game.
Levels are 100% linear with nothing to explore. This means that replayability potential is practically zero, unless you want to get achievemnts or play on a higher difficulty.
You play some kind of mutant who has the ability to rapidly regenerate all of his health as long as the damage wasn't lethal, without the need of any kind of medical aid, but this is typical to most military shooters these days.
Game does pose a reasonable challenge on Suicidal difficulty, encouraging you to aim for headshots and conserve ammo, and there is also a FUBAR difficulty for true masochists which unlocks after you complete the game.
I haven't encountered any technical issues running the game on max settings, no noticeable fps drops or anything like that. There aren't any issues with mouse control as well. This is a big plus compared to how bad console ports big companies tend to release (Watch Dogs / Deus Ex HR / etc.)
I think that this game is worth playing if you are even remotely interested, but it could have been a lot better.

Going to try and keep this one simple.
-If you liked N64-era Rare Ltd. games (Banjo-Kazooie, Banjo-Tooie, Donkey Kong 64) then you will most likely enjoy Yooka-Laylee
-If you did not enjoy N64-era Rare Ltd. games then you will most likely not enjoy Yooka-Laylee.
-If you enjoyed those N64-era Rare Ltd games but haven't experienced those 3D collectathon nuances in 15-20 years since they released then you will most likely be in for bumpy start and not care for Yooka-Laylee.
-This game was pitched as a 90s-era collectathon and an authentic 90s-era collectathon was delivered. There is no argument around this. Folks who are negative towards some of the gameplay design choices need to keep the original pitch in mind. The good and bad of 90s-era collectathon platformers is here. That’s what was pitched. That’s what was delivered. Plain and simple.

As far as truck simulations go, Euro Truck Simulator 2 just has to be the highest quality and most detailed I have played. After playing unmodded single player for a while it can get a bit repetative and boring over time, however, modding allows for pretty much anything to be achieved and adds whole new aspect of gameplay.
I have spent many, many hours in the ES2MP (Multiplayer) mod which allows thousands of players to truck in Europe together, this alone adds unpredicability and interaction that just wouldn't be possible with the AI in the game itself. Surprisingly, this game is nowhere near as boring as it looks and sounds. If they still had demos, you'd realize what I mean. Since you can stream internet radio into the game, it's a great way to catch up on the news or listen to podcasts in a somewhat relaxing environment. Not having driven anything larger than a box truck, I can't say how accurate the simulation is, but I can say it's not realistic, simply because all the trucks feel the same. Upgrading the engine makes it accelerate faster, and there are a few different chassis configurations, but the feel is barely impacted.
If you come at this game expecting a "king of the road" experience, like the blurb claims, you'll be disappointed. Even if you did feel like king of the road, your subjects (the other cars) have no personality or purpose other than to serve as obstacles. The way to think of this game is as a sort of zen-like experience. Once you get on the highway, turn on your favourite radio or podcast, and begin to relax, you'll see why I've spent over 100 hours pretending to drive shipments of toys around fake Europe.

Having played this game since alpha I can say that this is definitely worth your time. Klei is an excellent developer that delivers quality content and their plans and goals for this game are slowly and progressively coming to light. Like any game in early access there's always going to be bugs and crashes and current as of this update there is no tutorial, but the game is very well fleshed out and significantly more deep than you'll expect when you get in game. That predominantly is the biggest disconnect people have with this game. They expect either a casual simulation game which ONI is not, or they misunderstand the game mechanics and get frustrated when there is usually a simple solution to their problem. As the game ramps up in the future toward full release Klei does intend to flesh out a tutorial and make the complexities of the game a little more clear. Being active on the forums or in the fan Discord server really helps figuring out the meta. You can trust that that this game will continue to evolve in complexity and the good ol' quirky humor that comes with a Klei game.

First, this game is in alpha so expect bugs.  Many negative reviews are about bugs, this is in alpha.  If you have played game dev tycoon or develop games irl you know that smaller bugs are dealt with before the game is released, not while it is being made.  A lot of negative reviews also complain about how this has been in alpha state for a while now, and this is because the company literally consists of 10 employees at the moment with the lead developer doing a lot of the work.  They are creating really interesting updates to the game every month with such a small dev team.
Prison Architect is one of the few games on steam that uses the early access system very well.  Updates to the game are provided on a monthly basis, and they have just released Alpha 34 which includes basic gangs and commissary shops  (new room type).
The game plays like a mix between a tycoon style game and the sims, as you are building up the prison while the prison is running (unless you just want to design levels without prisoners being present, which is possible).  The darker subject material in comparison to most tycoon games that are lighthearted is definitely shown through a lot of the mechanics that have been included.
The price of the game is somewhat high at $30, however I think that it is worth it due to the constant updates it receives.      Steam Workshop is also very active for this game, which allows for you to transform the game into a whole new style of game (there are mods ranging from small modifications to a complete overhaul of the graphics and mechanics, like the star wars and gulag workshop mods).  The game is on sale a decent amount of the time, so if you are really pressed for cash you can wait for a sale to occur.

For a few quid, you can get this really well put together indie pool game.
8 and 9 ball pool await you, and each AI has it own set of challenges. Some of which I have yet to really master and get to grips with.
The tutorial section is quite a nice touch, so you're not just dumped in to the game having to figure out things like bank shots etc. Hell, I didn't even know it had a name until I played this game!
You can just whack the living bejesus out of the ball, but where's the skill in that??
Try bouncing the ball off the top edge of the table to hit the ball you need, or jumping over other balls to get the pot.
You've got, as near as I can tell, full control over the ball with spin, lockable power (nice touch!) and cue positioning. You can pull off some really bizarre moves.
Overall, this is a really nice game. Presented in a simple to understand format and graphically delicious. The AI characters have some, shall we say, odd traits. . I did giggle a little at Tiffany Bouvier, who'll eat you for breakfast. . Tiffany. Breakfast. . . At least it has a little bit of humour.
Music is quite nice, but a little repetative, especially in a long game. But at least you can skip the AI moves quickly.
I've been using mouse & keyboard to controll things and it's easy enough. I'll have to give my controller a try and see how I fair.
Only tiny tiny gripe I have, is every now and then it crashes. But, the devs are aware, and it should be fixed soon!
It would be nice to have a personal table baize as well as the included and DLC. Ah well, maybe the devs could peer in to that as well??
Overall, this rates highly in my list and has quickly been added to my favourites.

While Root really wasn't for me I think people who like more traditional first person shooters will enjoy the game quite a bit more than me.

If you are looking for a hard first person shooter I think you will enjoy Root even if the game didn't really appeal to me.

I see some people complaining that ROOT is either too hard or too slow, and the problem is pretty obvious that the haters are playing it wrong. Don't make the mistake of reading into the word "stealth" too much - at it's core, this game is a hardcore FPS in the vein of early Quake games, but the stealth is added as an option and adds a nice bit of variety to the gameplay. I've watched a couple video reviews and saw that there were some people that never tabbed out of stealth walking, so no wonder it took you 30 minutes to beat the first level. I made the same mistake when I first played it, relying on the stealth way too much, BUT if you combine the stealth options with the twitch shooter elements, the game starts to become far more apparent in how it should be played. I figured this out by accident on my second attempt after getting my♥♥♥♥♥♥wrecked 4 times playing like molasses, and it completely opened up my options. If I was running short on ammo, I'd go into stealth and club a guard to get some rounds, and if another guard turned the corner, I'd shoot him a couple times, hide, wait for him to come to me, and light him up. Use the cover to your advantage, that's what it's there for.
Overall, I'm thoroughly enjoying ROOT. It's kicking my♥♥♥♥♥still, but from what I can tell that's the entire point - it's a hardcore FPS, so if you're expecting some COD walk in the park, you're sorely mistaken, and if you're expecting Metal Gear, you're also sorely mistaken. Play the damn tutorial, you can get the "Skip the Tutorial" achievement later.
Pro Tip: Expect to die. A lot. Embrace it, enjoy it, adapt to it. It's Nintendo hard, get good.

I think Hitman (2016) is the lowest point in the franchises history.
Always online required, you are unable to play if the network is down, which happens quite alot.
Gameplay is basically of that of Hitman 5 Absolution, but you can walk around the level now. Ironically, this
game still feels linear in the way you have to do things.
The story is no longer engaging, Diana doesn't brief you as much as as the previous games, planning is very limited
You cant customize any weapons like you could in hitman blood money, which was my favorite.
Regarding gunplay, enemy AI have super human reaction time and 100% accuracy
The levels at first look huge, but in actuallity are very bland, empty spaces with standing npcs, with not much things to do.
There's basically training, then tutorial,a quick level then that's it.
In my opinion, Hitman fans with be sorely dissapointed, and I think newcomers should steer away from this game, and instead play the older titles , like Hitman 1, 2 and 4 to appreciate what Hitman was really about.
